gm.title: Description
lines: A golden-scaled Celestial that guards sacred places and watches over broad territories. Its lair is usually difficult to reach, such as a high pinnacle or a magically solid cloud.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). When the ki-rin fails a saving throw, it can spend a use to succeed instead.
Magic Resistance. The ki-rin has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Hoof attacks and one Horn attack, or make two Sacred Fire attacks.
Hoof. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d4 + 5) force damage.
Horn. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d8 + 5) radiant damage.
Sacred Fire. Ranged spell attack, +9 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. A hit deals 18 (3d8 + 5) radiant damage.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Wisdom (spell save DC 17) with no material components.
At will. Light, Major Image (6th level), Thaumaturgy.
3/day each. Cure Wounds, Dispel Magic, Lesser Restoration, Sending.
1/day each. Banishment, Calm Emotions, Create Food and Water, Greater Restoration, Plane Shift, Protection from Evil and Good, Revivify, Wind Walk.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The ki-rin has 3 legendary actions and regains spent uses when its turn starts. It can use one option immediately after another creature’s turn, paying the listed cost. It must be able to take actions and cannot do so before the end of its own first turn if surprised.
Move (1 action). Move up to half speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Smite (1 action). Make one Hoof, Horn, or Sacred Fire attack.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
At initiative count 20, losing ties, the ki-rin can use one option while in the lair and able to take actions. If surprised, it must finish its first turn first. Each option becomes available again after a long rest. The conjured objects appear 1 minute later at unoccupied spots the ki-rin chooses on the lair floor.
Create Comforts. Conjure permanent objects made of soft plant material, including manufactured goods, that collectively fit in a 20-ft. cube.
Create Stone and Metal. Conjure stone or metal objects that collectively fit in a 2-ft. cube. They vanish after 1 hour.
Create Wood. Conjure permanent wooden objects or objects made of comparably hard plant material that collectively fit in a 10-ft. cube.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Each effect can occur up to 3 miles from the lair.
Blessed Nature. Beasts, Plants, and Celestials become more vigorous and approach idealized forms. They rarely attack creatures they would not normally hunt.
Controlled Weather. The ki-rin can cast Control Weather in this area. The spell originates outdoors at the point nearest the lair’s center. It requires neither a clear path to the sky nor concentration to persist.
Pure Waters. The water runs pure. Deliberate contamination clears within 3 minutes.
Realm of Respite. Curses, diseases, and poisons are suppressed while affected creatures remain in the area, except for Aberrations, Fiends, and Undead.
Safe Descents. Creatures whose falls were not caused by the ki-rin or its allies descend at 60 ft. per round and take no falling damage. Aberrations, Fiends, and Undead fall normally.
On the ki-rin’s death, these effects end immediately, except the extra vigor of local flora and fauna lasts 3 years.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 162.

gm.title: References
lines: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 162 · https://5e.tools/bestiary.html#ki-rin_mpmm

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The ki-rin can turn a failed save into a success.
Magic Resistance. The ki-rin has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
Magic Weapons. The ki-rin's weapon attacks are magical.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Hoof attacks and one Horn attack.
Hoof. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (2d4 + 5) bludgeoning damage.
Horn. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 14 (2d8 + 5) piercing damage.

gm.title: Innate spellcasting
lines:
Use Charisma (spell save DC 17). These spells require no material components.
At will. Gaseous Form, Major Image (6th-level version), Wind Walk.
1/day. Create Food and Water.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
The ki-rin casts as an 18th-level cleric using Wisdom (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks).
Cantrips (at will). Light, Mending, Sacred Flame, Spare the Dying, Thaumaturgy.
Level 1 (4 slots). Command, Cure Wounds, Detect Evil and Good, Protection from Evil and Good, Sanctuary.
Level 2 (3 slots). Calm Emotions, Lesser Restoration, Silence.
Level 3 (3 slots). Dispel Magic, Remove Curse, Sending.
Level 4 (3 slots). Banishment, Freedom of Movement, Guardian of Faith.
Level 5 (3 slots). Greater Restoration, Mass Cure Wounds, Scrying.
Level 6 (1 slot). Heroes' Feast, True Seeing.
Level 7 (1 slot). Etherealness, Plane Shift.
Level 8 (1 slot). Control Weather.
Level 9 (1 slot). True Resurrection.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The ki-rin has 3 legendary actions. It can use one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It must be able to act. If surprised, it must finish its first turn before using one.
Detect (1 action). Make a Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom (Insight) check.
Smite (1 action). Make one Hoof attack or cast Sacred Flame.
Move (1 action). Move up to half speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

gm.title: Lair conjuration
lines:
While inside its lair, the ki-rin can use each of these options once per day.
Soft Plant Material. Permanently create enough objects made from soft plant material to fill a 20 ft. cube. This can include manufactured objects such as clothing, rope, and pillows.
Hard Plant Material. Permanently create enough objects made from wood or other hard plant material to fill a 10 ft. cube.
Stone or Metal. Create enough objects made from stone or metal to fill a 2 ft. cube. They vanish after 1 hour.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
These effects can occur within 3 miles of the lair. The effects end when the ki-rin dies, except that the vigor in plants and animals lasts 3 years.
Pure Water. Water stays pure. Deliberate contamination lasts no more than 3 minutes.
Vigor. Plants, animals, and good creatures grow toward ideal forms. They seldom attack creatures they would not normally hunt. Evil creatures find the holy atmosphere intolerable and usually stay away.
Suppression. Curses, diseases, and poisons affecting good creatures are suppressed within the area.
Control Weather. The ki-rin can cast Control Weather from anywhere within the area. The spell originates from the outdoor point nearest the lair's center. It can cast without a clear path to the sky and need not concentrate for the change to persist.
Gentle Winds. Winds support any falling non-evil creature if the ki-rin and its allies did not cause the fall. It descends 60 ft. per round and takes no falling damage.

gm.title: Description
lines: This feathered tyrannosaur hunts the ruins of Omu. Huge tracks and long scarlet, orange, and green feathers mark its amphitheater lair.

gm.title: Hit point rule
lines: The adventure fixes the King of Feathers at 200 hit points and gives no replacement Hit Dice expression.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Detect Invisibility. The king sees invisible creatures and objects as though they were visible.
Legendary Resistance (3/Day). When the king fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

gm.title: Innate spellcasting
lines: The king can cast Misty Step at will as a bonus action. It uses Wisdom and needs no components.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite and one Tail attack against different targets.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 33 (4d12 + 7) piercing damage. A Medium or smaller creature hit is grappled (escape DC 17) and restrained until the grapple ends. The king cannot bite another target while it holds that creature.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A colossal purple worm with armored segments, a fanged maw, and three long tongues.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Save Con +11. Immune to Charmed, Flanked, Frightened, and Prone. Blindsight 30 ft., Tremorsense 120 ft., passive Perception 10. No languages.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Multiple Tongues. Track three tongues separately. A tongue can be targeted by attacks only while it is grappling a creature. It has AC 20 and is immune to psychic damage. If it takes at least 35 damage in a single turn, it is destroyed and releases its captive. The worm regains destroyed tongues after a long rest. Damage to a tongue never damages the worm.
Slowed, Not Stopped (3/day). On a failed save, the worm can succeed instead. Each use reduces its speed and Tongue Grab reach by 10 ft. until it finishes a long rest, with a minimum of 5 ft. for each.
Tunneler. The worm can burrow through solid rock at half its burrowing speed, leaving a tunnel 10 ft. in diameter.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make up to one Tongue Grab per tongue the worm still has. Replace any number of these attacks with Swallow.
Tongue Grab. Melee weapon attack +14, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit 14 (4d6) acid damage and grapple the target (escape DC 19). That tongue is unavailable against other targets until the grapple ends.
Maw. Melee weapon attack +14, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 22 (3d8 + 9) piercing damage. A Huge or smaller target must succeed on a DC 19 Dexterity save or be swallowed as if by Swallow.
Swallow. Swallow a Huge or smaller creature the worm is grappling. The grapple ends. The swallowed creature is Blinded and Restrained, has total cover from outside attacks and effects, and takes 28 (8d6) acid damage at the start of each of the worm’s turns.
If a creature inside deals at least 30 damage to the worm in a single turn, the worm makes a DC 21 Constitution check at the end of that turn. On a failure, it disgorges every swallowed creature into empty spaces within 10 ft., where they land Prone. After the worm dies, a swallowed creature can spend 20 ft. of movement to escape and exit Prone.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Tongue Sweep. A creature the worm is grappling takes 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage. Each enemy within 10 ft. of that creature makes a DC 16 Dexterity save or takes the same damage.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Tongue Recall. When a tongue takes damage and survives, the worm can release its captive and retract the tongue. Attacks can target it again once it grapples a creature.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Each can be used once per encounter in any order after an enemy’s turn, at most one per round.
Open the Earth. Open a fissure starting at the worm, 20 ft. wide, 100 ft. long, and 40 ft. deep. Creatures in the area make a DC 19 Dexterity save. Failure drops them into the fissure for 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage and leaves them Prone. Success moves them to the closest unoccupied space outside the fissure.
Earth Breach. The worm burrows up to half its speed and bursts through the surface in a 10-ft.-radius circle. Each Huge or smaller creature in the circle makes a DC 19 Dexterity save or is swallowed as if by Swallow.
Better Out Than In. Creatures in a 60-ft. cone make a DC 19 Dexterity save against 21 (6d6) bludgeoning plus 21 (6d6) acid damage, halved on a success. The worm also ejects each swallowed creature, dealing 21 (6d6) bludgeoning damage to it and placing it Prone in an empty space of the worm’s choice in the cone.

gm.title: Encounter uses
lines: Use an existing fissure to stage the first tongue grab. Track tongue damage separately within each turn so the party can choose between freeing a captive and attacking the worm.

gm.title: Description
lines: The Codex Mortis destroyed the archaeologist Kiona Duemois’s body. She built an army of spectral undead to search for the lost book.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saving throws Int +9, Wis +6. Arcana +9, History +9, Perception +6. Resists acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from mundane attacks. Immune to necrotic and poison damage and to Charmed, Dazed, Exhaustion, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, and Unconscious. Blindsight 60 ft., passive Perception 16. Speaks Common, Draconic, and Orc.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Corrupting Phasing. Kiona can cross through creatures and objects. She takes 5 (1d10) force damage if she ends her turn inside an object. Each creature she passes through takes 9 (2d8) necrotic damage the first time she passes through it on a turn.
Incorporeal Empowerment. Incorporeal Undead ignore difficult terrain while within 120 ft. of Kiona.
Spiritual Sacrifice (3/day). After failing a save, Kiona can lose 15 HP and succeed instead.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Energy Siphon attacks.
Energy Siphon. Melee or ranged spell attack +9, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one creature. Hit 15 (3d6 + 5) necrotic damage. The target cannot regain HP until the start of Kiona's next turn. She gains temporary HP equal to half the damage dealt.
Rise from Death (1/day). Summon three shadows, two specters, or one wraith under Kiona's control. They appear in unoccupied spaces within 30 ft. and act immediately after her on the same initiative count.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Path of Pain. An incorporeal Undead other than Kiona within 120 ft. who can see her can move up to its speed.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Death’s Breath. After hitting Kiona with an attack from within 5 ft., the attacker must make a DC 17 Constitution save or be Poisoned through the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Kiona can use one of these actions after an enemy's turn, up to once per round. Each is available once per encounter, in any order.
Action 1, Restrain Them! Choose a visible point within 120 ft. Each enemy in a 20-ft.-radius sphere centered there makes a DC 17 Dexterity save. Failure leaves it Restrained until the end of Kiona's next turn.
Action 2, Ruinous March. Kiona and each ally within 60 ft. can move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Action 3, Vitality Drain. Kiona and each ally within 60 ft. can make a melee attack without using an action. A creature hit gains one level of Exhaustion.

gm.title: Mundane Attacks (MCDM)
lines: Magical and psionic attacks deal supernatural damage and bypass the listed resistance to mundane attacks.

gm.title: Recoverable Magic Item
lines:
Pathfinder’s Boots. Very rare. Attunement required. The wearer gains +2 AC and +10 ft. walking speed. The boots hold 7 charges. Spend 1 to cast Feather Fall, Jump, or Shield. They regain 1d6 + 1 spent charges at dawn.
Cursed Sentience. The item uses its Soulbinder's alignment, mental ability scores, and languages. It hears and sees in darkness within 60 ft. and can speak to its wearer telepathically. Break attunement with Remove Curse or equivalent magic. After seven days attuned and every 24 hours after that, make a DC 18 Wisdom save. Each failure reduces Wisdom by 1 while attuned. On the third failure, the Soulbinder takes control and changes the wearer's body, statistics, and equipment to match its own. The wearer remains aware. Breaking attunement restores the body and control. The Soulbinder returns to the item when attunement ends or the body dies. After 1d6 + 12 months of possession, the victim's soul and body are destroyed. The full group ritual for permanently lifting the curse is on p. 382.

gm.title: Actions

Full attack. One unarmed strike +11, katana +11/+6, or longbow +10/+5. Use the attack damage above.

gm.title: Supernatural abilities
lines:
Euphoria (Su). After at least a week of courtship and a successful Bluff (seduction) check, the woman makes a DC 20 Will save. Failure charms her as charm person (caster level 10th). She gains a +2 morale bonus on attack rolls and ability and skill checks near the kizoku, or takes a −2 morale penalty on those rolls when it is absent. This ends when the kizoku is destroyed or break enchantment dispels it.
Willow Heart (Su). After at least a month courting a euphoric woman and leading her to commit major betrayal or murder, the kizoku can offer a draining kiss. A failed DC 20 Will save lets it drain her life and turn her into a weeping willow as polymorph any object (caster level 10th). Ravenloft Innocents are immune to this death effect. While the kizoku lives, reversing the transformation leaves an inert body unless miracle, wish, or true resurrection restores the victim. After its death she can be restored normally, except that a victim whose tree provided the killing weapon still requires one of those three spells. The kizoku learns the languages spoken by those it drains and advances one Hit Die per four levels drained through this power.

gm.title: Spell-like abilities
lines: Caster level 10th, save DC 15 + spell level. At will: fly. 1/day each: alter self, calm emotions, charm person, color spray, command, confusion, crushing despair, daze, detect scrying, dimension door, disguise self, displacement, enthrall, gaseous form, hold person, hypnotism, invisibility, mind fog, mislead, rage, slow, and suggestion.

gm.title: Defenses and weakness
lines: DR 10/magic, low-light vision, regeneration 1, spell resistance 13. Its regeneration converts damage from ordinary attacks to nonlethal damage. Someone who truly loved a victim can identify her willow with a DC 20 Wisdom check. A weapon made from that willow’s heartwood deals lethal damage when used by that person. If they land the killing blow, the kizoku dies permanently and the stolen souls return to their owners. The kizoku normally tries to escape with its spells when threatened.

gm.title: Traps
lines:
Spiky Pit Trap. A 15-ft.-square trapdoor centered on the point opens onto a spiked pit 10 ft. deep. Each creature on the ground in that area makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. On failure, it falls in for 3 (1d6) piercing from spikes and 3 (1d6) bludgeoning from the fall. On success, move it to the closest unoccupied space outside the trapdoor.
Swarm of Bees Trap. Fill a cylinder 15 ft. in radius and 10 ft. high with bees. A creature first entering the swarm on a turn or starting a turn inside it makes a DC 12 Constitution save. Failure deals 5 (2d4) poison and leaves it Poisoned until the end of its next turn. Success halves damage and avoids the condition. At the start of each artifex turn, move the swarm 10 ft. straight away from the artifex. It disperses after 1 minute or when the artifex dies.
Wall of Fire Trap. Ignite a hidden trench to make an opaque wall 20 ft. long, 15 ft. high, and 1 ft. thick for 1 minute. On creation, creatures in it make a DC 12 Dexterity save against 7 (2d6) fire, taking half on success. A creature that enters the wall for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there takes 7 (2d6) fire.

lines:

Weapon Invention. Choose an option or roll 1d8. Each option can be used at most once per day.
1. Acid. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 5/20 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (2d6) acid damage.
2. Alchemist’s Fire. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 5/20 ft., one target. On a hit, the target takes 2 (1d4) fire damage at the start of each of its turns until it spends an action and succeeds on a DC 10 Dexterity check to extinguish the flames.
3. Basket of Centipedes. Throw the basket into a 5-ft. square within 20 ft. A Swarm of Centipedes emerges with 11 hit points and rolls initiative. It has a 50 percent chance to disperse at the end of each of its turns.
4. Green Slime Pot. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 5/20 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d10) acid damage and coats the target in slime, which deals 5 (1d10) acid damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can use an action to scrape or wash the slime away.
5. Rot Grub Pot. Break the pot in a 5-ft. square within 20 ft. A Swarm of Rot Grubs emerges and remains a hazard in that space.
6. Scorpion on a Stick. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 1 piercing damage. The target then makes a DC 9 Constitution save and takes 4 (1d8) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.
7. Skunk in a Cage. Release a skunk in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. It has AC 10, 1 hit point, a walking speed of 20 ft., and no effective attacks. It rolls initiative and on its turn uses its action to spray a random creature within 5 ft. The creature must pass a DC 9 Constitution save or be incapacitated by retching for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. A creature that does not need to breathe or is immune to poison succeeds automatically. The skunk must finish a short or long rest before spraying again.
8. Wasp Nest in a Bag. Throw the bag into a 5-ft. square within 20 ft. A Swarm of Wasps emerges with 11 hit points and rolls initiative. It has a 50 percent chance to disperse at the end of each of its turns.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

lines: A secretive fey that can tunnel through rock and bind intruders with rope made from its own hair.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Stone Camouflage. The korred has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in rocky terrain.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two attacks, choosing Greatclub or Rock for each.
Greatclub. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage, or 19 (3d8 + 6) if the korred is on the ground.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +9 to hit, range 60/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage, or 19 (3d8 + 6) if the korred is on the ground.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Wisdom (spell save DC 13), without any components.
At will. Commune with Nature, Meld into Stone, Stone Shape. Commune with Nature takes an action for the korred.
1/day. Otto's Irresistible Dance.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Command Hair. The korred has at least one 50-ft. rope woven from its hair. Choose one such rope within 30 ft. and command it to move up to 20 ft. and entangle a visible Large or smaller creature. Unless the creature succeeds on a DC 13 Dexterity save, the rope grapples it (escape DC 13). It is restrained for as long as the grapple lasts. The korred can release it as a bonus action. The grapple also ends if the korred dies or becomes incapacitated.
Hair rope. The rope has AC 20 and 20 hit points. At the start of each of the korred's turns, the rope regains 1 hit point if it still has at least 1 hit point and the korred is alive. The rope is destroyed at 0 hit points.

gm.title: Magical hair
lines: When cut, hair from a korred's head turns into the material of the cutting tool. A korred uses iron shears to make strands it can weave into iron ropes.

lines: Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse, p. 166.

gm.title: Description
lines: A reclusive fey that knows stone and ore. Korreds meet weekly to dance and beat out rhythms on stone with their clubs and hooves.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Stone Camouflage. The korred has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide in rocky terrain.
Stone's Strength. The korred rolls two extra damage dice with each weapon attack it makes while on the ground. Its attacks below include those dice.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
The korred uses Wisdom for its innate spells (spell save DC 13) and supplies no components.
At will. Commune with Nature, Meld into Stone, Stone Shape.
1/day each. Conjure Elemental (cast at 6th level, summoning only a galeb duhr, gargoyle, earth elemental, or xorn), Otto's Irresistible Dance.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Greatclub attacks or two Rock attacks.
Greatclub. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 10 (1d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage, or 19 (3d8 + 6) if the korred is on the ground.
Rock. Ranged weapon attack, +9 to hit, range 60/120 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage, or 24 (4d8 + 6) if the korred is on the ground.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines:
Command Hair. The korred has at least one 50-ft. rope made from its hair. It can command one such rope within 30 ft. to move up to 20 ft. and entangle a Large or smaller creature it can see. On a failed DC 13 Dexterity save, the rope grapples the target (escape DC 13). The target is restrained for as long as the grapple lasts. The korred can release the target as a bonus action. The target is also freed if the korred dies or becomes incapacitated.
Hair rope. The rope has AC 20 and 20 hit points. It recovers 1 hit point at the start of each of the korred's turns if it has at least 1 hit point and the korred is alive. At 0 hit points, the rope is destroyed.

gm.title: Magical hair
lines: When cut, hair from the korred's head becomes the material that cut it. Korreds use iron shears to make the strands for their iron ropes.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious. The kraken can breathe air and water. Freedom of Movement. The kraken ignores difficult terrain, and magical effects can’t reduce its speed or cause it to be restrained. It can spend 5 feet of movement to escape from nonmagical restraints or being grappled. Siege Monster. The kraken deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Multiattack. The kraken makes three tentacle attacks, each of which it can replace with one use of Fling. Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 23 (3d8 + 10) piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature grappled by the kraken, that creature is swallowed, and the grapple ends. While swallowed, the creature is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the kraken, and it takes 42 (12d6) acid damage at the start of each of the kraken’s turns. If the kraken takes 50 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the kraken must succeed on a DC 25 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall prone in a space within 10 feet of the kraken. If the kraken dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse using 15 feet of movement, exiting prone. Tentacle. Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit: 20 (3d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 18). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained. The kraken has ten tentacles, each of which can grapple one target. Fling. One Large or smaller object held or creature grappled by the kraken is thrown up to 60 feet in a random direction and knocked prone. If a thrown target strikes a solid surface, the target takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was thrown. If the target is thrown at another creature, that creature must succeed on a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw or take the same damage and be knocked prone. Lightning Storm. The kraken magically creates three bolts of lightning, each of which can strike a target the kraken can see within 120 feet of it. A target must make a DC 23 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

gm.title: Legendary Actions
lines: The kraken can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature’s turn. The kraken regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn. Tentacle Attack or Fling. The kraken makes one tentacle attack or uses its Fling. Lightning Storm (Costs 2 Actions). The kraken uses Lightning Storm. Ink Cloud (Costs 3 Actions). While underwater, the kraken expels an ink cloud in a 60-foot radius. The cloud spreads around corners, and that area is heavily obscured to creatures other than the kraken. Each creature other than the kraken that ends its turn there must succeed on a DC 23 Constitution saving throw, taking 16 (3d10) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A strong current disperses the cloud, which otherwise disappears at the end of the kraken’s next turn.

gm.title: Description
lines: An ancient leviathan that sinks fleets and draws sailors into the depths. It may live in a deep ocean trench, a sunken cavern, or a freshwater lake.

gm.title: Languages
lines: Understands Abyssal, Celestial, Infernal, and Primordial. Cannot speak. Telepathy 120 ft.

gm.title: Damage immunities
lines: Lightning and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The kraken breathes both air and water.
Freedom of Movement. It ignores difficult terrain. Magic cannot reduce its speed or restrain it. It may spend 5 ft. of movement to free itself from a nonmagical restraint or a grapple.
Siege Monster. It deals double damage to objects and structures.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three Tentacle attacks. The kraken can replace any of them with Fling.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 23 (3d8 + 10) piercing damage. A Large or smaller creature hit by this attack is swallowed if the kraken is already grappling it. Swallowing ends the grapple. The swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects originating outside the kraken, and takes 42 (12d6) acid damage at the start of every kraken turn. If a creature inside the kraken deals at least 50 damage to it in a single turn, the kraken makes a DC 25 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On failure it regurgitates every swallowed creature. They land prone in a space within 10 ft. of the kraken. If the kraken dies, its victims are no longer restrained by it and can spend 15 ft. of movement to crawl out of the corpse, landing prone.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +17 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. Hit 20 (3d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage. The target is grappled, escape DC 18, and restrained for as long as the grapple lasts. Each of its ten tentacles can hold one target.
Fling. Throw one Large or smaller held object or grappled creature up to 60 ft. in a random direction. The target lands prone. If it hits a solid surface it takes 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage per 10 ft. thrown. If the kraken throws it at a creature, that creature makes a DC 18 Dexterity save. Failure deals the same damage and knocks it prone.
Lightning Storm. Make three magical lightning bolts. Choose for each a target the kraken can see within 120 ft. A target makes a DC 23 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) lightning damage on failure or half on success.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The kraken has 3 legendary actions. It spends them on one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn and regains them at the start of its own turn. It cannot take them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it waits until after its first turn.
Tentacle Attack or Fling (1 action). Make one Tentacle attack or use Fling.
Lightning Storm (2 actions). Use Lightning Storm.
Ink Cloud (3 actions). Underwater, release ink in a 60-ft. radius. It spreads around corners and heavily obscures the area for everyone except the kraken. Another creature that ends its turn in the cloud makes a DC 23 Constitution save, taking 16 (3d10) poison damage on failure or half on success. A strong current disperses the ink. Otherwise the cloud dissipates at the end of the kraken's next turn.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, after any turns tied at 20, the kraken can choose one effect. It cannot do so while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it waits until after its first turn.
Current. Each creature within 60 ft. of the kraken makes a DC 23 Strength save. Push it up to 60 ft. away on failure or 10 ft. away on success.
Lightning Vulnerability. Creatures in water within 60 ft. of the kraken gain vulnerability to lightning damage until initiative count 20 of the next round.
Electrified Water. All creatures within 120 ft. make a DC 23 Constitution save, taking 10 (3d6) lightning damage on failure or half on success.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Within 6 miles of the lair, the kraken can change the weather at will as with Control Weather.
Water elementals form within 6 miles. They remain in the water and each has Intelligence and Charisma 1, with a modifier of -5.
Aquatic creatures within 6 miles with Intelligence 2 or lower are charmed by the kraken and act aggressively toward intruders.
All regional effects end immediately when the kraken dies. A creature assuming the kraken's form gains none of its legendary actions, lair actions, or regional effects.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Monster Manual (2014), pp. 196–197. Official errata revises the saving throw modifiers, Bite and Tentacle attack bonuses, nonmagical attack wording, and general legendary creature rules.

gm.title: Description
lines: These immense tentacled titans were weapons of the gods. They rise from deep lairs to rip through fleets and coastal settlements.

gm.title: Languages
lines: understands Abyssal, Celestial, Infernal, and Primordial but can't speak; telepathy 120 ft..

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. Breathes air and water.
Legendary Resistance (4/day, 5/day in its lair). It can turn a failed save into a success.
Siege Monster. Deals double damage to structures and objects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks, then use Fling, Lightning Strike, or Swallow.
Tentacle. Melee attack, +17 to hit, reach 30 ft. Hit deals 24 (4d6 + 10) bludgeoning damage. One of the ten tentacles Grapples its target (escape DC 20) and Restrains it until the grapple ends.
Fling. Throw a Large or smaller creature Grappled by the kraken into a visible space within 60 ft. that is not in the air. The thrown creature and all creatures in that space make DC 25 Dexterity saves. Failure deals 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage and leaves the target Prone. Success halves the damage and avoids the condition.
Lightning Strike. One visible creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 23 Dexterity save. Failure deals 33 (6d10) lightning damage and success halves it.
Swallow. One creature Grappled by the kraken makes a DC 25 Dexterity save. Failure deals 23 (3d8 + 10) piercing damage. A Large or smaller target that fails is also swallowed and its grapple ends. The kraken can have up to four creatures swallowed. A swallowed creature is Restrained, has Total Cover against outside attacks and effects, and takes 24 (7d6) acid damage at the start of each of its own turns.
When a creature inside deals at least 50 damage to the kraken in a single turn, the kraken makes a DC 25 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On failure, every swallowed creature is expelled and falls Prone within 10 ft. If the kraken dies, swallowed creatures stop being Restrained. They can spend 15 ft. of movement to escape the corpse and exit Prone.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
3 uses (4 in its lair). Spend one use immediately after another creature’s turn. Recover all uses at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Storm Bolt. Use Lightning Strike.
Toxic Ink. Use while underwater. Each creature in a 15-ft. Emanation from the kraken makes a DC 23 Constitution save. Failure leaves it Blinded and Poisoned until the end of the kraken’s next turn. The kraken then moves up to its Speed. It cannot use this option again until the start of its next turn.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Ocean Tyrant. Beasts are Charmed while within 1 mile of the lair.
Sea and Storms. In its lair, the kraken can cast Control Weather using Intelligence and without spell components.
Both effects end immediately if the kraken dies or its lair moves.

gm.title: Description
lines: The Titan of the Mindstorm sleeps beneath the ocean east of Higara. It can hold and crush a ship with its mind.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Saving throws Con +16, Int +18, Wis +14. Arcana +18, History +18, Perception +14. Immune to cold, lightning, psychic, and thunder, to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from mundane attacks, and to Blinded, Charmed, Dazed, Flanked, Frightened, Poisoned, Paralyzed, Petrified, and Stunned. Blindsight 120 ft., truesight 60 ft., passive Perception 24. Understands all languages but cannot speak. Telepathy 150 ft.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. Breathes air and water.
Discorporation. At 0 HP or death, all conditions and other effects end. The Kraken teleports to its resting place, returns to life with full HP, and falls Unconscious.
Siege Monster. Deals double damage to objects and structures.
Slowed Resistance (3/day). Turn a failed save into a success. Each use reduces the Kraken's speed by a cumulative 10 ft. for 24 hours.
Supernatural Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells, powers, and other supernatural effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make four Tentacle attacks or use Mental Lance three times.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, 30-ft. reach, one target. Hit 19 (2d10 + 8) bludgeoning plus 11 (2d10) psychic damage and Grappled (escape DC 18). Each of its ten tentacles can grapple one target.
Mental Lance (3rd-order power). Ranged power attack, +18 to hit, 120-ft. range, one creature. Hit 22 (4d10) psychic damage and the target is Frightened of the Kraken until the start of the Kraken's next turn.
Psionic Storm. Restrain one vehicle the Kraken sees within 120 ft. The effect ends if its concentration breaks as for a spell or if the Kraken and the vehicle are more than 120 ft. apart. If three of the Kraken's turns end while the effect lasts, the vehicle drops to 0 HP and the effect ends.
Skull-Splitting Howl (1/day). Enemies within 120 ft. make DC 26 Constitution saves. On a failure, each takes 55 (10d10) psychic damage and cannot concentrate on powers or spells until the start of the Kraken's next turn. A success halves the damage.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Telekinetic Fling. Throw one creature the Kraken is grappling into an unoccupied space it sees within 60 ft. The creature lands Prone and takes 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Psychic Reprisal. When an attack damages the Kraken, its enemies within 30 ft. of the attacker, including the attacker, make DC 26 Wisdom saves. Failure deals 22 (4d10) psychic damage, halved on a success.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Each action is available once per encounter, after an enemy finishes a turn. Use them in any order, at most one per round.
1. Psionic Tentacles. Conjure tentacles that make a Tentacle attack against each enemy within 120 ft. The Kraken then uses Telekinetic Fling on each creature it is grappling.
2. Psionic Ink. Teleport up to 60 ft. to an unoccupied space the Kraken sees. Each creature within 30 ft. of the space it left makes a DC 26 Dexterity save. On a failure, the creature is covered in ink and takes 16 (3d10) psychic damage at the start of each turn until it uses an action to wipe the ink away.
3. The Ocean's Wrath. Creatures within 120 ft. make DC 26 Wisdom saves. Failure deals 65 (10d12) psychic damage and makes the creature Frightened of the Kraken for 1 minute, with a repeat save at the end of each turn. A success halves the damage and avoids the condition.

gm.title: Description
lines: A lightly built, winged reptilian warrior. Krolli settle in isolated eyries and sometimes travel to trade or take mercenary work.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Hill or mountain. Rare, active at any time. Omnivore. Intelligence 8–12. Treasure M, with A listed for the community. Any alignment. Appearing 1d20. No magic resistance. Height 7–8 feet, wingspan 17–20 feet. Elite morale 13–14.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Ground attacks. Make two claws for 1d8+1 each and a bite for 1d6+1.
Airborne attacks. Make two front claws for 1d8+1 each, one rear claw for 1d10, and a bite for 1d6+1. Krolli can use this sequence against targets on the ground.
Weapons. About 30% fight with weapons instead, and many carry shields.

gm.title: Flight and defenses
lines: The table lists AC 3 (2). Wings are AC 7. Frontal attackers can target the wings only if taller than the krolli, and rear attackers always roll against wing AC. A krolli that has lost at least half its HP cannot fly. It carries up to 30 pounds in flight unencumbered and up to 45 pounds encumbered. Save vs. paralyzation every 15 minutes of unencumbered flight or every 5 minutes when encumbered. On failure it must land and rest 1 hour per 15 minutes already flown.

gm.title: Group encounters
lines: An eyrie holds 3d20 adults, including one 7th-level fighter per 10 adults, and young with 1/2 HD equal to about one-tenth the adult count. The prose assigns 95% of krolli to fighters up to 7th level and 5% to likely priests of Ka. Krolli have acute senses and speak a dialect of Shazak, with Common rare among the lizard kin.

gm.title: Red Curse and XP
lines: Krolli in cursed areas can acquire Legacies and use cinnabryl to avoid Affliction. The XP table gives 270 normally, 420 with a Legacy, and 650 for a leader.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: AC 2 is parenthetical in the table. The prose mentions shields without explicitly tying them to that number. The XP column prints an extra 650 with a Legacy without marking which tier it belongs to.

gm.title: Description
lines: An amphibious Underdark warrior with a net and an adhesive shield. Kuo-toa can bring deities into being through shared belief.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A fishlike humanoid with bulging eyes and rubbery skin.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. It breathes air and water.
Otherworldly Perception. It senses any Invisible creature or creature on the Ethereal Plane within 30 ft. It can pinpoint those that are moving.
Slippery. It has advantage on ability checks and saving throws to escape a grapple.
Sunlight Sensitivity. In sunlight it has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that use sight.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit for 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.
Spear. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit for 4 (1d6 + 1) piercing damage, or 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage with two hands in melee.
Net. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 5/15 ft., one Large or smaller creature. A hit leaves the target Restrained. A creature can spend an action to free itself or another creature with a successful DC 10 Strength check. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the AC 10 net destroys it and frees the target unharmed.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Sticky Shield. When a creature misses the kuo-toa with a melee weapon attack, the kuo-toa catches the weapon with its shield. The attacker must succeed on a DC 11 Strength saving throw to keep the weapon from sticking. A stuck weapon is unusable. The wielder is Grappled while it is stuck if the wielder can't or won't release it. A creature can take an action and make a DC 11 Strength check to pull the weapon free.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Spear uses the higher damage only in two-handed melee. Net attacks at +3, range 5/15 ft., and Restrain one Large or smaller creature on a hit. An action and a successful DC 10 Strength check free the creature. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the net (AC 10) destroys it and frees the target unharmed.

lines: A former scout who serves the Order of the Ouroboros as a covert assassin. She keeps some of her petrified targets in her courtyard.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Saves Str +8, Dex +11, Con +9, Wis +7. Skills Athletics +8, Deception +8, Perception +7, Persuasion +8, Stealth +11, Survival +7. Immune to poison damage and the Poisoned condition. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 17. Common and Elvish.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Stone Sacrifice (3/day). Emer can turn a failed save into a success by ending her Stone Gaze on a creature of her choice within 300 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use Pinning Shot or make three attacks in any combination of Snake Bite and Longbow. Also use Stone Gaze or Envenomed Stone if available.
Snake Bite. Melee weapon attack +11, reach 10 ft., one creature. Hit 17 (5d6) poison damage. On a failed DC 17 Constitution save the target is Poisoned and cannot take reactions until the end of Emer's next turn.
Longbow. Ranged weapon attack +11, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit 11 (1d8 + 7) piercing plus 14 (4d6) poison damage.
Pinning Shot. Make three Longbow attacks against a creature touching the ground within 150 ft. Two or more hits Restrain it with arrows. The target or a creature that can reach it can use an action to remove the arrows and end the effect.
Stone Gaze. Up to three visible creatures within 60 ft. make DC 17 Constitution saves. A first failure starts petrification, reduces speed by 10 ft., and gives disadvantage on Dexterity checks and saves. While turning to stone, an end-of-turn save ends the effect. If targeted by another Stone Gaze, a second failure cuts speed by another 10 ft. and Dazes the target. A third failure Petrifies the target and removes its repeat saves. Stone Sacrifice, Cure Ailment of at least 4th order, Greater Restoration, or a similar supernatural effect can reverse the completed petrification.
Envenomed Stone (Recharge 5–6). Each creature within 60 ft. turning to stone from Stone Gaze makes a DC 17 Constitution save, taking 44 (8d10) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Mesmerizing Eyes. Choose one creature Emer can see within 60 ft. that can also see her. On a failed DC 17 Wisdom save, it is Charmed until the start of its next turn and must immediately spend its reaction, if available, to move up to its speed in a direction Emer chooses.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Blinding Mucus. When a creature Emer can see within 5 ft. hits her with a melee attack, that creature must pass a DC 17 Dexterity save or take 7 (2d6) acid damage and become Blinded until the start of its next turn.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Each villain action is available once per encounter. Use one at most per round, in any order, immediately after an enemy's turn.
1. I See You! Use Stone Gaze on every visible enemy within 60 ft.
2. Medusa's Evolution. Gain a flying speed of 40 ft. for 1 minute, then move up to speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
3. Stone Puppets. Emer and each creature turning to stone from her Stone Gaze move up to their speeds and each make a weapon attack against a creature Emer chooses, without an action.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: On its turn a Dazed creature can move, take an action, or take a bonus action. It chooses one. Becoming Dazed during its turn ends the turn. Extra actions from effects such as Haste or Action Surge are still available. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration can remove Dazed.

Pinning Shot. Make three Longbow attacks against a creature touching the ground within 150 ft. Two or more hits Restrain it with arrows. The target or a creature that can reach it can use an action to remove the arrows and end the effect.
Stone Gaze. Up to three visible creatures within 60 ft. make DC 17 Constitution saves. A first failure starts petrification, reduces speed by 10 ft., and gives disadvantage on Dexterity checks and saves. While turning to stone, an end-of-turn save ends the effect. If targeted by another Stone Gaze, a second failure cuts speed by another 10 ft. and Dazes the target. A third failure Petrifies the target and removes its repeat saves. Stone Sacrifice, Cure Ailment of at least 4th order, Greater Restoration, or a similar supernatural effect can reverse the completed petrification.
Envenomed Stone (Recharge 5–6). Each creature within 60 ft. turning to stone from Stone Gaze makes a DC 17 Constitution save, taking 44 (8d10) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Mesmerizing Eyes. Choose one creature Emer can see within 60 ft. that can also see her. On a failed DC 17 Wisdom save, it is Charmed until the start of its next turn and must immediately spend its reaction, if available, to move up to its speed in a direction Emer chooses.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Blinding Mucus. When a creature Emer can see within 5 ft. hits her with a melee attack, that creature must pass a DC 17 Dexterity save or take 7 (2d6) acid damage and become Blinded until the start of its next turn.

gm.title: Villain Actions
lines:
Each villain action is available once per encounter. Use one at most per round, in any order, immediately after an enemy's turn.
1. I See You! Use Stone Gaze on every visible enemy within 60 ft.
2. Medusa's Evolution. Gain a flying speed of 40 ft. for 1 minute, then move up to speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
3. Stone Puppets. Emer and each creature turning to stone from her Stone Gaze move up to their speeds and each make a weapon attack against a creature Emer chooses, without an action.

gm.title: Dazed (MCDM)
lines: On its turn a Dazed creature can move, take an action, or take a bonus action. It chooses one. Becoming Dazed during its turn ends the turn. Extra actions from effects such as Haste or Action Surge are still available. Cure Ailment, Lesser Restoration, and Greater Restoration can remove Dazed.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Haze-native creatures
lines:
Printed source. Appendix A, pp. 196–197. These traits leave the creature’s CR as printed. They apply to Haze natives and exclude creatures recruited or summoned by the party.
Fully Contaminated. Immune to contamination and has advantage on saves against contaminated spells.
Haze Adaptation. Can benefit from a long rest in the Haze. It can see twice as far through the Haze and Deep Haze.
Haze Dependence. Gains one Exhaustion level for each 24 hours outside the Haze. It can remove those levels only in the Haze.
Delerium Healing. As an action, touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) HP. That shard cannot heal this way again for 24 hours.

gm.title: Description
lines: A lebendtod plays the part of the same worker or neighbor it was in life. When its master calls, the disguise drops and the entire household can turn on intruders.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any land on Graben Island. Solitary, pair, family of 5–8, or community of 40–60. Always neutral evil. Standard treasure. Advances by character class. The sample is a 2nd-level human commoner. Knows its languages from life.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative −1. AC −1 Dex, +2 natural, and +2 leather armor. Touch 9, flat-footed 14. Base attack +1, grapple +2. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +0, Ref −1, Will +2.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +6, Disguise +8, Profession (farmer) +5, Sense Motive +4. Iron Will (bonus), Skill Focus (Disguise).

gm.title: Traits
lines: DR 10/magic and undead traits. Lifespan runs ten times that of the base creature. It normally fights only on its master’s orders.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +2 melee for 1d4 + 1 or sickle +2 melee for 1d6 + 1. Full attack makes two claws +2 melee for 1d4 + 1 each and a bite −3 melee for 1d3 + 1, or uses the sickle.
Detachable Limbs (Ex). It can remove or reattach any extremity unharmed as a standard action and still sense and control it when detached. Seeing it take off its head or use an arm as a club prompts a DC 15 Horror save except for the most callous witnesses.
Disguise Self (Sp). Twice per day at caster level 12, assume its appearance on the day it died. A free action maintains the disguise indefinitely. Magical or supernatural damage ends it immediately.
Create Spawn (Su). As a full-round action that provokes attacks of opportunity, breathe into the mouth of a dying humanoid below 0 HP as the target takes its last breath. Isolate the body for 72 hours. It rises as a lebendtod if left untouched, or as a ghast with none of its former abilities if disturbed but largely intact. Either serves the lebendtod’s master until that master dies.

gm.title: Adapting the encounter
lines: For a different humanoid base, keep its size, speed, base attack, saves, and skill points. Make it undead, convert Hit Dice to d12, add +2 natural armor, and add missing claw and bite attacks. Claw/bite base damage from Fine through Colossal: none/none, 1/none, 1d2/1, 1d3/1d2, 1d4/1d3, 1d6/1d4, 2d4/1d6, 2d6/1d8, 2d8/2d6. Use better existing damage. Str +2, Dex −2, Int −2. Remove Con. Add Iron Will and +5 racial bonuses to Bluff and Disguise. CR increases by 1. A clerical lebendtod rebukes instead of turning and cannot rebuke its master or the master’s other lebendtod.

lines: DR 10/magic appears in the sample stat block. The general template does not list it as a benefit.

gm.title: Description
lines: A banished tanar’ri posing as a red steel weapon. It steals Legacies through the wielder until it can return home.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any terrain. Very rare, solitary, active at any time. Feeds on Legacies. Intelligence 19–20. No treasure. Chaotic evil. Appearing 1. Magic resistance 25%. True leech form is 7 feet long. Fearless morale 19–20.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Weapon form. The unattended leech moves and makes one attack each round using the damage of the weapon it resembles. Once held, it uses the wielder’s weapon abilities. It can appear as a +1 rapier, dagger, magical hook, or pistol. It may also let the wielder use an absorbed Legacy.

gm.title: Bond and theft
lines:
An intelligent creature that takes hold of the weapon is bonded as tendrils enter its flesh, with no save. The leech vanishes into its host until it reappears in one of its weapon shapes. The host drops anything held in that hand.
To steal a Legacy it does not have, the leech makes the host plunge its blade into the heart of a just-killed creature. The host can refuse a demand with a Wisdom check, blocking the leech for an hour or until a new conflict. During theft the host may save vs. spell to expel the leech, at −1 per Legacy it has absorbed. A host dies immediately once the leech steals 15 Legacies while bonded to that same host.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Starts with 1d4+1 acquired Legacies and never needs cinnabryl. Its weapon form radiates evil. A good priest’s grasp makes it wrench free at effective Strength 20. It will not choose a host with a heroic spirit. A paladin can still grasp it.

gm.title: Restored tanar’ri
lines: At 20 absorbed Legacies, the leech can break its banishment. It spends two rounds attacking those present before it automatically gates home. In this form it makes two claws for 4d4 each, casts as a 9th-level wizard, and is immune to cold, fire, electricity, poison, and charm.

gm.title: Description
lines: The missing queen-consort lives in the gardens of Queen’s Park. She covers her face with a cracked porcelain mask.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Deception +5, Insight +4, Perception +4, Stealth +5. Darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 14. Common.

gm.title: Base stat block
lines: Medusa, SRD 5.1 (2014 fifth-edition rules). Queen’s Park replaces the inherited Petrifying Gaze and actions with Radiant Gaze and Tentacle Hair.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Radiant Gaze. When a creature that can see Lenore’s eyes starts its turn within 30 ft. of her, she can force a DC 14 Constitution save if she is not Incapacitated and can see it. Failure deals 22 (4d10) radiant damage and adds one contamination level. Success halves the damage.
Avert Eyes. Unless Surprised, a creature can look away at the start of its turn to avoid the save. It cannot see Lenore until its next turn starts, when it can avert its gaze again. If it looks at her early, it immediately saves against the gaze.
Own Reflection. If Lenore sees herself in a polished surface within 30 ft. while in bright light, she is Blinded and Incapacitated for 1d6 hours.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Tentacle Hair. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing and 14 (4d6) necrotic damage. The target makes a DC 14 Constitution save and gains one contamination level on failure.

gm.title: Encounter notes
lines: Her attendants use Dryad statistics. Her own likeness and the names of her lost family provoke her.

gm.title: Delerium contamination
lines:
Printed source. Appendix C, pp. 222–223.
Add contamination levels from each exposure. A contaminated character rolls 1d20 at the end of each long rest and gains one level on a 1.
Symptoms are cumulative. Level 1 has no symptom. Level 2 halves healing from Hit Dice. Level 3 prevents HP recovery from a long rest. Level 4 halves damage the creature deals with weapon attacks and spells. Level 5 makes it Incapacitated. Level 6 triggers Monstrous Transformation.
After a character gains a level, roll 1d6. On a result at or below the current level, the GM chooses a new mutation or rolls on the printed mutations table. Replace or reroll duplicate mutations.
Contamination does not wear off. Purge Contamination can remove levels and causes Exhaustion. Heal removes all contamination and mutations. Each level removed also removes one random mutation. At level 0, all symptoms and mutations end.
A contaminated humanoid rises as a Haze Husk 24 hours after death. It rises as a Haze Wight if it had at least six class levels or Hit Dice. Raising a creature from the dead reduces its contamination by one level.
Monstrous Transformation. At level 6 or higher, the creature transforms after one round. Replace its statistics, hit points, and Hit Dice with those of a monster the GM chooses. Contamination resets to 0, and the GM controls the transformed creature.
Wish or similar magic can restore one transformed creature, clearing its madness and contamination. Using Wish this way gives the caster a 33 percent chance of losing the ability to cast it again.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The encounter replaces the Medusa’s actions. Tentacle Hair is its only printed replacement.

Animate Spirits (2/day). Animate two Shades in unoccupied spaces she can see within 30 ft. They act immediately after her on the same initiative count and follow her verbal commands. They are destroyed if she dies.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Ethereal Step (3/day). When a creature Lestheris can see within 60 ft. targets her with an attack, spell, or power while she is outside the Ethereal Plane, she can teleport up to 60 ft. to an unoccupied space she can see or enter the Ethereal Plane. If she enters that plane, she returns at the start of her next turn to the space she left. If that space is occupied, she chooses a nearest unoccupied space.

gm.title: Utility Spells
lines: Intelligence, save DC 14. At will: Mage Hand, Message, Minor Illusion. 3/day each: Detect Magic, Mage Armor. 1/day each: Knock, Speak with Dead. Each takes 1 action.

gm.title: Villain Party Action
lines:
Grave Order. The party can use one villain party action per round, after an enemy finishes its turn. It can use each action once per encounter, in any order. The creature performing the action must be present and able to act (not Incapacitated).
Action 5, The Tide of Death. For each enemy Lestheris can see within 30 ft., animate one Shade in an unoccupied space she can see within 30 ft. They follow the turn order, command, and destruction rules under Animate Spirits.

gm.title: Description
lines: A vast serpent formed from water. It can drag ships under or flood a settlement along the coast.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). After failing a saving throw, the leviathan can choose to succeed.
Partial Freeze. If the leviathan takes at least 50 cold damage during one turn, both of its speeds drop to 20 ft. and it has disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn.
Siege Monster. The leviathan deals double damage to objects and structures.
Water Form. The leviathan can enter and stop in a hostile creature's space. It can pass through openings at least 1 inch wide without squeezing.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Slam attack and one Tail attack.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (2d12 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 13 (2d12) acid damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +14 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (2d10 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (3d6) acid damage.
Tidal Wave (recharge 6). Magically send a wave out from a visible point within 120 ft. The wave can reach up to 250 ft. long, 250 ft. tall, and 50 ft. wide. Each creature in it makes a DC 24 Strength save. It takes 45 (7d12) bludgeoning damage and falls prone on a failure. A success halves the damage and avoids falling prone. Water spreads along the ground in all directions, extinguishes unprotected flames in the wave's area and within 250 ft. of that area, and vanishes.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The leviathan has 3 legendary actions and regains spent actions at the start of its turn. It can use one option at the end of another creature's turn. It needs to be able to act and, if surprised, can spend them only after its first turn ends.
Move (costs 1 action). Move up to the leviathan's speed.
Slam (costs 2 actions). Make one Slam attack.

gm.title: Description
lines: A leviathan rises out of deep water on the scale of a moving flood. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The leviathan can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Partial Freeze. If the leviathan takes at least 50 cold damage in one turn, all its speeds become 20 ft. and it has disadvantage on attacks until the end of its next turn.
Siege Monster. The leviathan deals double damage to objects and structures. The Tidal Wave rules already account for this trait.
Water Form. The leviathan can enter and stop in a hostile creature's space. It can pass through gaps at least 1 inch wide without squeezing.
Elemental Nature. It needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Slam and one Tail attack.
Slam. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (1d10 + 10) bludgeoning damage plus 5 (1d10) acid damage.
Tail. Melee weapon attack, +16 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 16 (1d12 + 10) bludgeoning damage plus 6 (1d12) acid damage.
Tidal Wave (Recharge 6). While submerged, the leviathan creates a wall of water centered on itself. The maximum dimensions are 250 ft. long, 250 ft. high, and 50 ft. thick. When the wall appears, each other creature in it makes a DC 24 Strength save and takes 33 (6d10) bludgeoning damage on a failure or half as much on a success. At the start of each of the leviathan's following turns, the wall and the creatures in it move 50 ft. away from the leviathan. Each Huge or smaller creature already in the wall or whose space it enters must pass a DC 24 Strength save or take 27 (5d10) bludgeoning damage. This moving-wall damage applies at most once per creature per turn. After each turn when the wall moves, the wall loses 50 ft. of height and the damage it deals in later rounds drops by 1d10. The wall vanishes at 0 ft. A creature caught in the wave must pass a DC 24 Strength (Athletics) check to swim during its turn.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The leviathan has 3 legendary actions and regains them at the start of its turn. Use only one option at a time, at the end of another creature's turn.
Slam (2 actions). Make one Slam attack.
Move (1 action). Move up to the leviathan's speed.

lines: Liara commands the Flaming Fist garrison at Fort Beluarian. She helps adventurers who serve the fort's interests and takes a share of the Jahaka pirates' profits.

lines:
Brave. Liara has advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
Flaming Fury. Once per turn, when Liara hits with a melee weapon, she can add 10 (3d6) fire damage to the hit.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three melee attacks.
Battleaxe. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) if wielded in two hands.
Heavy Crossbow. Ranged weapon attack, +3 to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d10 + 1) piercing damage.

gm.title: Fort Beluarian
lines: An exploration charter costs 50 gp, credited toward the Flaming Fist's claim on half the expedition's proceeds and discoveries. Charter holders can hire up to six guards at 1 gp per guard per tenday. Liara uses a Sending Stone to pass ship manifests and sailing schedules to Zaroum Al-Saryak. In exchange, the Jahaka pirates leave Baldur's Gate ships alone.

gm.title: Roleplaying
lines: She values obedience, has sworn to hold the fort for Grand Duke Ulder Ravengard, and has little pity for those unable to defend themselves.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Tomb of Annihilation, appendix D, p. 227, and chapter 2, pp. 54–56 (Fort Beluarian).

lines: The lich can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature’s turn. The target must succeed on a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw against this magic or become frightened for 1 minute. Each non-undead creature within 20 feet of the lich must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw against this magic, taking 21 (6d6) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

gm.title: Description
lines: An undead wizard whose phylactery anchors its soul. A lich can keep artifacts and spellbooks close at hand while hiding the phylactery elsewhere.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). The lich can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Rejuvenation. If its phylactery still exists when the lich is destroyed, a new body forms within 5 ft. of it in 1d10 days. The lich returns with full HP.
Turn Resistance. The lich has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead.
Undead Nature. The lich doesn't need air, food, drink, or sleep.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
18th-level wizard spellcaster. Intelligence is its spellcasting ability (save DC 20, +12 to hit). The following spells are prepared.
At will (cantrips). Mage Hand, Prestidigitation, Ray of Frost.
1st level (4 slots). Detect Magic, Magic Missile, Shield, Thunderwave.

7th level (1 slot). Finger of Death, Plane Shift.
8th level (1 slot). Dominate Monster, Power Word Stun.
9th level (1 slot). Power Word Kill.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Paralyzing Touch. Melee spell attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit 10 (3d6) cold damage. The target makes a DC 18 Constitution save or is Paralyzed for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the paralysis on a success.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
The creature has 3 legendary actions and spends them one option at a time at the end of another creature's turn. It regains them at the start of its turn. It can't use them while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Cantrip (1 action). Cast one cantrip.
Paralyzing Touch (2 actions). Use Paralyzing Touch.
Frightening Gaze (2 actions). Choose one visible creature within 10 ft. It makes a DC 18 Wisdom save against this magic or is Frightened for 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. After it succeeds or the effect ends, it is immune to this gaze for 24 hours.
Disrupt Life (3 actions). Each non-undead creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 18 Constitution save against this magic. Failure deals 21 (6d6) necrotic damage. Success halves it.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
In its lair the lich is CR 22 (41,000 XP). On initiative count 20, losing ties, choose one option that was not used the previous round. The creature can't use a lair action while incapacitated or otherwise unable to act, or before its first turn if surprised.
Recover a Spell Slot. Roll 1d8. Regain one spent spell slot of the rolled level or lower. If no spent slot qualifies, the action has no effect.
Negative Energy Tether. Link to a visible creature within 30 ft. Whenever the lich takes damage, the target makes a DC 18 Constitution save. On a failure the lich takes half the damage, rounded down, and the target takes the remainder. The link ends on initiative count 20 of the next round or when either creature leaves the lair.
Spirits of the Dead. Call apparitions of creatures that died in the lair to attack one visible creature within 60 ft. It makes a DC 18 Constitution save. Failure deals 52 (15d6) necrotic damage. Success halves it. The apparitions vanish after the attack.

gm.title: Phylactery
lines:
Feed the Phylactery. If the lich casts Imprisonment for this purpose, it can trap the body and soul of one target in its phylactery in place of the usual imprisonment options. The lich and phylactery must be on the same plane, and the phylactery holds only one creature at a time.
Dispel Magic cast on the phylactery with a 9th-level slot releases its prisoner. After 24 hours inside, the prisoner is consumed and only divine intervention can restore them to life.
The phylactery may require a particular ritual, item, or weapon to destroy. The print leaves that requirement to the DM. Imprisonment is part of the printed phylactery procedure and does not appear in this stat block’s prepared spell list.

gm.title: Description
lines: A lich binds its soul to a hidden spirit jar. It can outlast the loss of its body while that jar remains intact.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (4/day, 5/day in its lair). It can turn a failed save into a success.
Spirit Jar. If destroyed while it has a spirit jar, the lich returns at full HP after 1d10 days. Its new body appears in an unoccupied space in its lair.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make three attacks in any combination of Eldritch Burst and Paralyzing Touch.
Eldritch Burst. Melee or ranged attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. Hit deals 31 (4d12 + 5) force damage.
Paralyzing Touch. Melee attack, +12 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit deals 15 (3d6 + 5) cold damage and leaves the target Paralyzed until the start of the lich’s next turn.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
Cast one of these spells as an action, using Intelligence (spell save DC 20).
At will. Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Dispel Magic, Fireball (level 5), Invisibility, Lightning Bolt (level 5), Mage Hand, Prestidigitation.
2/day each. Animate Dead, Dimension Door, Plane Shift.
1/day each. Chain Lightning, Finger of Death, Power Word Kill, Scrying.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Protective Magic. Cast Counterspell or Shield when the chosen spell’s trigger occurs. Use the same spellcasting ability and save DC as Spellcasting.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
3 uses (4 in its lair). Spend one use immediately after another creature’s turn. Recover all uses at the start of this creature’s turn. It cannot use these actions while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act.
Deathly Teleport. Teleport up to 60 ft. to a visible unoccupied space. Each creature within 10 ft. of the space left behind takes 11 (2d10) necrotic damage.
Disrupt Life. Each non-Undead creature in a 20-ft. Emanation from the lich makes a DC 20 Constitution save. Failure deals 31 (9d6) necrotic damage and success halves it. After using this option, wait until the start of its next turn before using it again.
Frightening Gaze. The lich casts Fear using Intelligence (DC 20), as in its Spellcasting action. It can't use this option again until the start of its next turn.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
All-Seeing. In its lair the lich can cast Clairvoyance with no components, using the ability listed under Spellcasting.
Inevitable Siphon. The lich consumes the soul of any Humanoid that dies within 1 mile of its lair. Only True Resurrection or Wish can bring that Humanoid back to life.
Both effects end immediately if the lich is destroyed or moves its lair. They return if the lich gains a new body through Spirit Jar.
