lines: Solitary, always neutral evil, no treasure. May appear in any environment.

gm.title: Dread elemental rules
lines:
Printed source. Elemental, Dread, p. 63, and Mists subtype, pp. 7–8.
In Ravenloft, calling a standard elemental has a 20% chance of producing a dread elemental. Summoning magic always produces the dread form. Accidental dread elementals are uncontrolled, and the Dark Powers supply the matching materials. Intentional conjuring requires the matching material and uses the usual chance for the elemental to break control.
Dread elementals understand speech but do not communicate. Their Mists subtype makes them native throughout Ravenloft and allows them to be summoned in any domain. A dismissed dread elemental returns to Ravenloft itself, so the realm's restrictions on calling do not break the calling pact.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Infuse Evil prints the Will DC without a base 10. Using its printed formula, the tier DCs are 1, 3, 6, 11, 14, and 17. Its printed Fortitude DC stays 15.

gm.title: Description
lines: This skeletal ferryman herds travelers deeper into the Mists. If subdued, it may trade passage for its freedom.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Misty border and fogbanks on any land. Solitary. Always neutral evil. No treasure. Advancement 6–9 HD (Large). No level adjustment listed. Can communicate with any creature that has a language.

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +7. AC +3 Dex and +4 natural, touch 13, flat-footed 14. Base attack +2, grapple +4. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +1, Ref +4, Will +6.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Undead traits, +2 turn resistance, damage reduction 5/magic. Obscuring Mist (Su). When summoned within a domain, obscuring mist at caster level 12th remains centered on it. It vanishes if that mist is dispelled. Mist does not obscure the ferryman’s own vision.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +4 melee (1d6 + 2 plus ferryman’s rot). Full attack. Two claws +4 each and bite −1 melee (1d8 + 1); each hit can transmit rot.
Ferryman’s Rot (Su). Injury disease. DC 15 Fortitude, incubation 1 week, initial damage 1d4 Con. It persists until remove disease or similar magic cures it, or the victim reaches Constitution 0 and dies. An afflicted victim who dies rises as a mist ferryman after 6 rounds and retreats into the Mists.
Summoning Howl (Ex). When outmatched, call 1d8 + 1 other ferrymen. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and help until combat ends.

gm.title: Summoned ferryman
lines: Someone can conjure it with summon monster VII, but it attacks the summoner. If incapacitated, it can bargain for release by taking itself and all adjacent creatures to a requested spot in Ravenloft, as with greater teleport.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The special-attack summary says mist poison, while the attacks and detailed rules use ferryman’s rot. Ongoing damage is not listed separately. Use the 3.5 disease timing and the printed 1d4 Constitution damage on a failed daily save as a table default, while preserving the exception to natural recovery.

gm.title: Description
lines: A construct forms out of the Mists, wearing the face of the person whose attempt to create it went wrong.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +8. AC −1 size, +2 Dex, +9 natural. Touch AC 11, flat-footed AC 18. Base attack +13, grapple +21. Space 10 ft., reach 10 ft. Fort +11, Ref +8, Will +11.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +21 melee for 3d6 + 8. Full attack makes two slams at the same bonus and damage.
Infuse Essence (Su). A critical hit that kills the target turns it into a mist horror. Finding and capturing that creature is required before restoring the victim to life. A target that survives becomes ethereal and unable to act for 10 rounds. Damage directed at the golem goes to that victim instead. Direct physical attacks against the victim require a magic weapon. If the victim dies during the effect, it becomes a mist horror.
Mist Door (Su). The golem spends the round doing nothing else, and attacks against it gain +2. It retreats into the Mists the following round, leaving thick fog that clears after an hour.
Mournful Howl (Su). Anyone within 50 ft. must make a DC 15 Will save or flee in terror. The howl is audible up to a mile away.
Ram (Ex). Its blows against structures work like a battering ram.
Spellshroud (Sp). The mist extends 15 ft. beyond the golem and produces one of ten spells per use, each usable once per day. When surprised, it releases a random unused effect. Use each spell's usual save type with a −4 penalty to its DC. Roll 1d10 if needed: 1 cloudkill, 2 confusion, 3 blindness, 4 hold person, 5 Tasha's hideous laughter, 6 Otto's irresistible dance, 7 stinking cloud, 8 silence, 9 vampiric touch, 10 slow.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Damage reduction 10/magic. Mists subtype. The Demiplane of Dread is its home plane. In foggy conditions its targets take −2 initiative.
Magic Immunity (Ex). Immune to spells, spell-like abilities and supernatural effects. Damage-dealing spells heal 1 HP per 2 damage they would normally deal if the golem is injured. Dispel magic has no effect.
Construct traits. Immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, disease and similar effects. Critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability damage, energy drain and death from massive damage do not affect it, subject to the exceptions below.

gm.title: Dread golem commands
lines: The creator can give commands from within 60 ft. if the golem can see and hear them. It follows the last command and responds to attacks against it. Some dread golems act independently.

gm.title: Specific Focus (Ex)
lines: At creation, its focus was exposed to moonlight within 50 ft. of both golem and creator. The object weighs at most 5 lb. and is worth at least 10,000 gp. A holder can command five tasks. The golem cannot harm the holder while they carry the item. It follows instructions literally and increasingly twists their intent. After the fifth task, the focus vanishes and appears elsewhere in Ravenloft. The golem then hunts its former holder.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Climb +11, Hide +6, Jump +12, Listen +4, Move Silently +6, Spot +4, Survival +4. Alertness, Blind-Fight, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Power Attack.

gm.title: Encounter details
lines: Any terrain in the Mists. Solitary, always chaotic evil, no treasure. Advances to 19–23 HD (Huge) or 24–30 HD (Gargantuan).

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The prose gives no duration for the howl’s flight and no caster level or base save DC for Spellshroud. The header labels +13/+21 as Base Attack. Use the second value as grapple, following the adjacent stat blocks.

gm.title: Description
lines: A ripple stalks travelers in the Mists. It gathers into a shape, sometimes borrowing the thing its victim fears most.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Printed common example based on a 5th-level human rogue. Ravenloft Mists, solitary, neutral evil, no treasure. Advancement 6–9 HD (Medium), 10–14 HD (Large).

gm.title: Combat statistics
lines: Initiative +6. AC 13 (+1 Dex, +2 natural). Base attack +2, grapple +5 as printed. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +1, Ref +5, Will +2. Climb +8, Disable Device +7, Hide +14, Listen +10, Move Silently +13, Open Locks +10, Spot +14. Alertness, Balance, Blind-Fight, Improved Initiative, Stealthy.

gm.title: Traits
lines: DR 10/magic, incorporeal and undead traits, and +5 turn resistance in the sample. Immune to holy water, charm, spells that normally affect undead, and spells that need a physical body, such as blindness/deafness. SR 10 applies to spells cast within 20 ft. and leaves spell-like abilities and spell-producing magic items unaffected.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Slam +5 melee (2d6 + 3). Full attack: two slams at +5, each for 2d6 + 3. The published sample lists sneak attack 3d6 + 3.
Assemble. It takes 1d4 turns to form a body capable of attacking. Until formed, creatures in the Mists can detect the hint of its presence with DC 20 Spot. The horror can break off combat by dispersing and must then spend another 1d4 turns reassembling.
Telempathic Projection (Sp). Send emotions or short messages to anyone within 120 ft. who is in the Mists. DC 15 Will lets a recipient resist or ignore it. A common horror stays in one area and may send false reassurance to make travelers pause while it assembles.

gm.title: Wandering mist horror
lines: Uses the common horror’s statistics, can roam the Mists and actively seeks prey. Fear Aura (Su), once daily: everyone within 120 ft. makes a DC 15 Fear check. It uses the aura early, in the first normal combat round if it surprised the targets. Suggestion (Sp), once daily: one creature within 120 ft. makes a DC 15 Will save to resist a telepathic suggestion.

gm.title: Creating a Mist Horror
lines: Apply to a living creature. Keep size, base attack, saves, and skill points, and change type to undead with the original type augmented. All present and future Hit Dice become d12. Give fly 30 ft. or retain a faster base fly speed. Keep base natural armor and add deflection equal to the higher of +1 or its Cha modifier. Replace ordinary attacks with natural attacks and keep the base special attacks and qualities. Add DR 10/magic, the immunities, SR 10, projection, and +4 turn resistance. Remove Con, add +2 Cha, and give +4 racial bonuses to Hide, Move Silently, and Spot. Keep skills usable in incorporeal form and add Improved Initiative and Stealthy. CR is base +1. Any evil, solitary, no treasure, no level adjustment, and the sample’s advancement ranges.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The encounter sample retains Con 15, natural armor without a deflection bonus, and +5 turn resistance. The template removes Con, adds deflection, and grants +4 turn resistance. Use the displayed numbers for the printed sample.

The projection rule specifies a DC 15 Will save. The common horror’s tactics instead mention an opposed Will check when it offers false reassurance. Use the listed DC for a quick ruling. The template prints 'average good' maneuverability. Use good, as in the encounter sample.

gm.title: Damage vulnerabilities

gm.title: Traits

lines: The Sewn Sisters' silent servant lays out a feast in the Trial of the Pentagon. An illusion makes him look like a gaunt man in a worn black suit.

gm.title: Languages

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned, unconscious.

gm.title: Traits
lines:

Construct Nature. He does not need air, food, drink, or sleep.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Claw attacks.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (2d4 + 1) slashing damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom save or remain frightened until the end of his next turn.
Terrifying Glare. Choose one creature he can see within 30 ft. If it can see him, it must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom save or become magically frightened until the end of his next turn. The target is paralyzed while frightened by the glare.

gm.title: Pentagon trial
lines: Detect Magic reveals the illusion. Dispel Magic exposes his true form with a successful DC 16 check. He attacks only in response to an attack or at the hags’ command. He carries their Hag Eye, the key to the cage in area 71, and a black marble that activates the Ebon Pool in area 81.

gm.title: Description
lines: The Witchlight Carnival’s reserved co-owner used to tend a clock tower in Gloomwrought under the name Naeryx Krumple. His pocket watch can pack up the carnival or set it in motion.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Fey Ancestry. Witch has advantage on saves against being charmed. Magic cannot put him to sleep.
Special Equipment. Witch carries and is attuned to the Witchlight Watch.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Cane attacks.
Cane. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, one target within reach 5 ft. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning damage plus 6 (1d12) necrotic damage.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
While carrying the Witchlight Watch, use an action to cast one spell with Intelligence (save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). No spell components are needed.
At will. Fire Bolt, Invisibility, Message. After casting Invisibility, roll a d8. On a 3 or 8, Witch loses access to Invisibility until the next dawn.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Blessing of the Raven Queen (1/day). Teleport up to 30 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space. Witch takes all worn or carried equipment with him, looks ghostly, and has resistance to all damage until the start of his next turn.

gm.title: Encounter notes
lines: Witch and Mister Light keep the carnival running under the Hourglass Coven’s pact. The Witchlight Watch lets Witch start a one-hour magical setup or takedown as an action while he and the carnival are on the same plane. This moves the carnival’s objects and leaves creatures free to move safely.

lines: A quick-witted thief in Valor’s Call, Molliver gives most of their spoils to people in need. They often act first and count on friends to get them out of trouble.

gm.title: Description
lines: The former ruler of Malbolge seeks a way to reclaim his title.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Cold. Bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks that are not silvered.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Legendary Resistance (3/day). After failing a save, Moloch can choose to succeed instead.
Magic Resistance. Moloch has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Regeneration. Moloch regains 20 hit points at the start of his turn. Radiant damage prevents this healing at the start of his next turn. He dies only if he starts his turn at 0 hit points and fails to regenerate.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite, one Claw, and one Many-Tailed Whip attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 26 (4d8 + 8) fire damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 17 (2d8 + 8) force damage.
Many-Tailed Whip. Melee weapon attack, +15 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d4 + 8) lightning damage plus 11 (2d10) thunder damage. On a failed DC 24 Strength save, a creature is pulled up to 30 ft. straight toward Moloch.
Breath of Despair (Recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 30-ft. cube must pass a DC 21 Wisdom save or take 27 (5d10) psychic damage, drop whatever it is holding, and become frightened of Moloch for 1 minute. On each of its turns while frightened in this way, it must Dash and move away from Moloch by the safest route available. If it has nowhere to move, it can skip the Dash. At the end of its turn, it can repeat the save if it has no line of sight to Moloch, ending the fear on a success.
Teleport. Teleport up to 120 ft. to an unoccupied space Moloch can see, taking any equipment he wears or carries.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Charisma (spell save DC 21). No material components are required.
At will. Alter Self (Moloch can become Medium when changing his appearance), Confusion, Detect Magic, Fly, Major Image, Stinking Cloud, Suggestion, Wall of Fire.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
Moloch has 3 legendary actions. Spend the listed cost to use one option at the end of another creature's turn. He regains spent actions at the start of his turn. He must be able to act and, if surprised, must first finish his first turn.
Attack (1 action). Make one Bite, Claw, or Many-Tailed Whip attack.
Teleport (1 action). Use Teleport.
Cast a Spell (2 actions). Use Spellcasting.

gm.title: Demon summoning mechanics
lines: Summon Demon (1/day, optional). As an action, choose 1d6 babaus, 1d4 chasmes, or one marilith. The attempt has a 50% chance to succeed. gm.title: Description
lines: A morkoth collects treasures, secrets, and captives on an island that drifts between the planes. Its prized possessions are kept in the island’s central sanctum.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Amphibious. The morkoth can breathe air and water.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Bite attacks and one Tentacles attack, or make three Bite attacks.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) slashing damage plus 10 (3d6) psychic damage.
Tentacles. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (3d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage. A Large or smaller creature is grappled (escape DC 14) and restrained until the grapple ends. It takes 15 (3d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns. The morkoth cannot use Tentacles against another target while it holds this creature.
Hypnosis. Each creature in a 30-ft. cone of magical energy makes a DC 17 Wisdom save. On a failure, it is charmed by the morkoth for 1 minute and must try to get as close to the morkoth as possible, using its actions to Dash until within 5 ft. It can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns and whenever it takes damage, ending the charm on a success. When a creature succeeds on a save or the effect ends for it, it has advantage on saves against this morkoth's Hypnosis for 24 hours.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Intelligence (spell save DC 17). No material components are required.
At will. Detect Magic, Mage Hand.
3/day each. Darkness, Dimension Door, Dispel Magic, Lightning Bolt, Sending.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Spell Reflection. When the morkoth succeeds on a save against a spell or a spell attack misses it, choose a different creature the morkoth can see within 120 ft. The chosen creature becomes the target in its place and can be the caster. That creature makes its own save, or the spell's attack roll is rerolled against it, as appropriate.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
On initiative count 20, losing ties, the morkoth can choose one option while in its lair and able to act. If surprised, it must first finish its first turn. Its lair profile is CR 12 (8,400 XP).
Cast a Spell. Cast Darkness, Dispel Magic, or Misty Step using Intelligence without spending a spell slot.
Hypnotize. Use Hypnosis from a point within 120 ft. of the morkoth. It can use a point it cannot see.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
The effects below end immediately if the morkoth dies.
Alter Water. With no action, the morkoth can change the water in its lair. One minute later, it becomes clear and breathable like air or returns to normal water of any clarity.
Locate Creatures and Objects. The morkoth notices new creatures and objects on the island or in its sanctum. As an action, it can locate one creature or object on the island. Visitors feel watched.
Lost Possessions. A creature that has been on the island for under a year must make a DC 10 Intelligence save after each short or long rest. On a failure, it misplaces a possession. A player chooses what their character loses. A DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check can recover the concealed item nearby. After 1 hour, any unrecovered item reaches the lair, where its owner easily recognizes it.
Supernatural Lure. While in its lair and not incapacitated, the morkoth can switch the lure at its entrances on or off at any time. A creature within 30 ft. of an enchanted entrance that can see it must make a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure, it must use its movement each turn to enter and head straight toward the morkoth without realizing that it is approaching a creature. It can repeat the save when it first sees the morkoth, at the end of each of its turns, and whenever it takes damage. A success ends the effect.

Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (2d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Tentacles. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (3d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage and grapples a Large or smaller creature (escape DC 14). While grappled, the target is restrained and takes another 15 (3d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of the morkoth’s turns. The morkoth cannot use Tentacles on another target until the grapple ends.
Hypnosis. Each creature in a 30-ft. cone makes a DC 17 Wisdom save against the magical effect. On a failure, the morkoth charms the creature for 1 minute. The charmed target tries to get as close to the morkoth as it can. It uses its actions to Dash until it is within 5 ft. of the morkoth. The target can save again at the end of each of its turns or when it takes damage, ending the effect on a success. A creature that succeeds on its save or is no longer under the effect has advantage on saves against this morkoth’s Hypnosis for 24 hours.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Spell Reflection. When the morkoth succeeds on a save against a spell or a spell attack misses it, choose another creature it can see within 120 ft., including the caster. The spell targets that creature in its place. The new target makes its own save or the spell attack is rerolled against it.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
In its lair, the morkoth is CR 12 (8,400 XP). At initiative count 20, losing ties, it can use one of the following options.
Hypnosis. Use Hypnosis from a point within 120 ft. The morkoth can pick a point it cannot see.
Cast a Spell. Cast Darkness, Dispel Magic, or Misty Step using Intelligence and without expending a spell slot.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Island Watch. The morkoth notices new creatures and objects arriving on its island or within its sanctum. As an action, it can find the location of one creature or object on the island. Visitors feel watched during their stay.
Lost Possessions. When a creature that has spent less than a year on the island finishes a short or long rest, it makes a DC 10 Intelligence (Investigation) check. On a failure, one possession goes missing. A player chooses what their character loses. The object stays hidden nearby and can be found on a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. An hour later, an unrecovered object arrives in the morkoth’s lair. The owner immediately recognizes it there and can easily recover it.
Lure. While in its lair and not incapacitated, the morkoth can turn the enchantment on its entrances on or off at any time. A creature that can see an enchanted entrance within 30 ft. must make a DC 15 Wisdom save. On a failure, it uses its movement on each of its turns to enter and take the most direct route toward the morkoth without knowing where the urge leads. It can save again on seeing the morkoth, at the end of each of its turns, and whenever it takes damage, ending the effect on a success.
Alter Water. The morkoth can change the water in its lair with a thought. The change takes 1 minute and requires no action. It can make the water as clear and breathable as air or return it to ordinary water, clear or murky.
These effects end immediately when the morkoth dies.

gm.title: Lycanthrope encounter rules
lines:
Printed source. Lycanthrope, pp. 137 and 148.
Alternate Form (Su). Where available, take or leave an animal or hybrid form as a standard action. Equipment does not change. Entering either form heals as a day of rest. A slain lycanthrope returns to humanoid form where it has one, but severed parts keep their animal shape. An afflicted creature normally gains one alternate form and can struggle to control it.
Curse of Lycanthropy (Su). A qualifying bite to a humanoid within one size category requires Fortitude DC 18 or transmits the curse. Bludgeoning or nonpenetrating attacks cannot transmit it. Afflicted lycanthropes can spread it in Ravenloft. The general text specifies animal form, but a listed hybrid curse also uses this procedure at the table. Use any strain-specific exception below.
Natural lycanthropes generally have DR 10/silver in animal or hybrid form, while afflicted ones have DR 5/silver. Some strains name a different material. Low-light vision and scent work in any form unless the profile specifies otherwise. Lycanthropic empathy allows simple communication, gives a +4 racial bonus on attitude checks with the corresponding normal or dire animal, and permits simple commands to friendly animals.
A spellcaster cannot use verbal, somatic, or material components in animal form and cannot use verbal components in hybrid form. Apply the printed encounter stats for each form.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The human attack is printed at +0 despite its +4 base attack. Keep the printed attack. The dire wolf and hybrid quality lines omit low-light vision, which the general rule grants in every form.

gm.title: Mouth of Chaos mechanics
lines:
Roll 1–3. Make three Fist attacks against one random creature within reach. With no creature in reach, gain advantage on all attack rolls until the end of the giant’s next turn.

Roll 6–7. Make one Bite attack against a random creature in reach. With no other creature in reach, the giant is stunned until the start of its next turn.
Roll 8–10. Make one Bite and two Fist attacks against one random creature within reach. With no creature in reach, gain advantage on all attack rolls until the end of the giant’s next turn.

lines: Azalin’s muddy undead rise from the marsh with damaged or missing limbs. They drag anyone caught in both claws into the mud coating their chests.

lines: Initiative −1. AC 12 (+2 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 12. Base attack +2, grapple +7. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +1, Ref +3, Will +4. Listed skills are Combat Reflexes +4, Hide +4, Use Rope +4, Search +4. Toughness.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack. Claw +7 melee for 1d6 + 5 damage. Full attack. Two claws at +7, each for 1d6 + 5.
Disease (Ex). A claw injury calls for a DC 15 Fortitude save. Failure deals 1 Strength damage initially, then 1 Strength damage per day for 1d6 days.
Suffocate (Ex). Two claw hits against the same victim grab them. Starting next round, the victim may try a Strength check once per round, with DC equal to their own Strength score. On a failure they take 1d4 suffocation damage that round. A success frees them.

gm.title: Encounter details

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The stat line prints Charisma −10, puts Combat Reflexes +4 among the skills, and gives initiative −1 despite Dexterity 14. Combat Reflexes is a feat in 3.5. Use the printed attack-last procedure and keep the supplied AC, attack and save figures.

gm.title: Lair actions
lines:
In its lair the mummy lord is CR 16 (15,000 XP). At initiative count 20, losing ties, it can choose one effect and cannot repeat the previous round's effect. It cannot do so while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. If surprised, it must wait until after its first turn.
Each undead in the lair knows the exact location of every living creature within 120 ft. of itself until initiative count 20 next round.
Each undead in the lair has advantage on saves against effects that turn undead until initiative count 20 next round.
Until initiative count 20 next round, a non-undead creature attempting a spell of 4th level or lower in the lair feels pain and can choose a different action. If it tries to cast the spell, it makes a DC 16 Constitution save. On a failure it takes 1d6 necrotic damage per spell level, and the spell is wasted without effect.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines: Food brought into the lair molds instantly, water evaporates at once, and other nonmagical drinks spoil. A divination spell cast there by anyone other than the mummy lord has a 25 percent chance to give misleading results chosen by the DM. An existing chance of failure or unreliability increases by 25 percentage points. Anyone who takes treasure from the lair has disadvantage on every saving throw until the treasure is returned or Remove Curse or other magic lifts the curse. All regional effects end as soon as the mummy lord is destroyed.

gm.title: In its lair
lines: 15,000 XP, 4 uses of Legendary Resistance per day, and 4 Legendary Action uses.

gm.title: Regional effects
lines:
Cursed Fate. When a creature other than the mummy lord or its allies casts a Divination spell within 1 mile of the lair, it makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On failure, the spell has no effect and the action, Bonus Action, or Reaction used to cast it is spent. The caster keeps the resources it would have spent on the spell.
Soul Drain. Creatures within 1 mile of the lair have Disadvantage on Death Saving Throws.
Both effects stop immediately if the mummy lord is destroyed or relocates its lair. They resume when it forms a new body through Undead Restoration.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Words of Ancient Doom (group attack). Melee or ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, 5-ft. reach or 30-ft. range, one creature. Hit 4 necrotic damage. With at least three rotwraps participating, the target cannot speak or use telepathy until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

If the party is headed there, she asks them to recover it and can offer 250 gp worth of pieces from her treasury if pressed for a reward.

gm.title: Roleplaying
lines: She insists on the respect due her station and sees her pact as a way to protect Na and the aarakocra who sheltered them.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Necrotic Absorption. When Mycete would take necrotic damage, she regains that many HP instead.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Parasitic Spores. Melee or ranged spell attack, +5 to hit, 5-ft. reach or 30-ft. range, one target. Hit 7 (2d6) necrotic damage. Mycete heals 3 (1d6) HP if the target is a creature.
Fungal Growth. Pick a visible point within 60 ft. Solid surfaces in a 10-ft. square centered there become difficult terrain. A creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must pass a DC 13 Constitution save or be Poisoned for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Animate Husks (1/day). Three Rotting Zombies appear in unoccupied spaces Mycete can see within 30 ft. They go immediately after her on the same initiative count, obey her spoken commands, and perish if she dies.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Spore Eruption. Destroy a Rotting Zombie under Mycete's control. Each enemy within 5 ft. of it makes a DC 13 Constitution save, taking 9 (2d8) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success.

gm.title: Utility Spells
lines: Wisdom, spell save DC 13. At will: Druidcraft. Three times per day: Locate Animals or Plants. Once per day each: Fog Cloud, Pass Without Trace. Each takes 1 action.

gm.title: Villain Party Actions
lines: Grave Order action 4, Fungal Paradise. Use once per encounter after an enemy's turn while Mycete is present and not Incapacitated. The Grave Order uses at most one villain party action per round. Mycete destroys any number of her visible Rotting Zombies within 30 ft. Each explodes in a 10-ft.-radius sphere. Every creature within one or more explosions makes one DC 13 Constitution save, taking 5 (2d4) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success. The ground in each sphere gains the effects of Fungal Growth. If Mycete controls no Rotting Zombies within 30 ft., she uses Animate Husks instead without spending or needing a use.

gm.title: Description
lines: The largest myconid in a colony leads its circles and can animate corpses as spore servants.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A towering, broad-capped fungus that stands above the other myconids in its circle.

gm.title: Languages
lines: None. Rapport Spores allow telepathic communication.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Distress Spores. When the myconid takes damage, other myconids within 240 ft. sense its pain.
Sun Sickness. Sunlight gives it disadvantage on ability checks, attack rolls, and saves. More than 1 hour in direct sunlight kills it.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use either Hallucination Spores or Pacifying Spores, then make a Fist attack.
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, 5-ft. reach, one target. Hit 8 (3d4 + 1) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (3d4) poison damage.
Animating Spores (3/day). Release spores at one humanoid corpse or one corpse of a Large or smaller beast within 5 ft. After 24 hours it rises as a spore servant. It remains animated for 1d4 + 1 weeks or until destroyed. This action cannot animate the same corpse again.
Hallucination Spores. Choose one visible creature within 5 ft. It makes a DC 12 Constitution save. On a failure it is Poisoned and Incapacitated by hallucinations for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the effect on a success.
Pacifying Spores. Choose one visible creature within 5 ft. It makes a DC 12 Constitution save. On a failure it is Stunned for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns and ends the effect on a success.
Rapport Spores. Release spores in a 30-ft. radius. They spread around corners and affect creatures with Intelligence 2 or higher, excluding constructs, elementals, and undead. For 1 hour, affected creatures can speak telepathically to each other within 30 ft.

gm.title: Spore servant template
lines:
Use the template for a Large or smaller creature that once had flesh and blood. Keep its AC, HP, Hit Dice, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, vulnerabilities, resistances, and immunities. Its type becomes Plant, its tags fall away, and its alignment becomes unaligned. Reduce each speed by 10 ft., to a minimum of 5 ft. Set Intelligence to 2, Wisdom to 6, and Charisma to 1.
Remove the creature's original saving throw and skill bonuses, special senses, traits, and languages. Give it blindsight 30 ft., with blindness beyond that range, and immunity to Blinded, Charmed, Frightened, and Paralyzed. It takes orders through a myconid's Rapport Spores and prioritizes orders from the most powerful myconid.
Keep Multiattack and melee weapon attacks that deal bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. Drop any other damage types unless they come from equipment. If the servant cannot otherwise deal damage, it can make an unarmed strike for 1d4 + its Strength modifier bludgeoning damage, or 2d4 + its Strength modifier if Large.

lines: Cold, fire, lightning. Bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Demonic Shadows. The area within 10 ft. of the nabassu is dim light that nonmagical light cannot brighten.
Devour Soul. The nabassu can consume the soul of a creature it killed in the past hour, excluding Constructs and Undead. It spends at least 10 minutes within 5 ft. of the corpse, then gains d8 Hit Dice equal to half the slain creature’s Hit Dice. Roll the new dice and add their total to the nabassu’s hit points. Each four Hit Dice gained add 3 (1d6) damage to its attacks on a hit. The added dice, hit points, and damage last 6 days. Only Wish can bring the victim back to life.
Magic Resistance. The nabassu has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Claw attack, and use Soul-Stealing Gaze.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 38 (5d12 + 6) necrotic damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +11 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (4d10 + 6) force damage.
Soul-Stealing Gaze. Choose one visible creature within 30 ft., excluding Constructs and Undead. It makes a DC 16 Charisma save. On a failure, it takes 13 (2d12) necrotic damage. Lower its hit point maximum by the damage it took and restore half that amount to the nabassu. The reduction lasts until a short or long rest. The target dies if its maximum reaches 0. A Humanoid killed this way immediately rises as a ghoul controlled by the nabassu.

gm.title: Description
lines: A green hag who poses as Mbala's last survivor. She wants the nearby pterafolk driven out and prefers to lure victims away from their companions.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. She breathes air and water.
Mimicry. She can copy animal sounds or humanoid voices. A listener identifies the imitation with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check.

gm.title: Innate spellcasting
lines: Charisma, save DC 12. At will without material components, cast Dancing Lights, Minor Illusion, or Vicious Mockery.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Claws. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage.
Illusory Appearance. Use magic to disguise herself and her gear as a creature of similar size and humanoid shape. The illusion ends at her death or when she dismisses it as a bonus action. Physical contact exposes the disguise. A creature can also spend an action to study it and make a DC 20 Intelligence (Investigation) check.
Invisible Passage. She and her gear become magically invisible until she attacks, casts a spell, or loses concentration as though concentrating on a spell. She leaves no physical traces while invisible and can only be tracked by magic.

gm.title: Mbala allies
lines: Her whistle calls 2d6 Flying Monkeys that fetch food and supplies but refuse to fight for her. If she commands the Flesh Golem buried beside her hut to attack, it rises as a bonus action.

gm.title: Rite of Stolen Life
lines: The rite takes one hour and uses an intact or mostly intact humanoid corpse, a gemstone worth 100 gp or more, and the sacrifice of another humanoid. The sacrifice’s spirit reanimates the corpse and takes on its knowledge and personality. Restore the returned character to full HP and keep its statistics. Change its type to Undead and remove the need to eat, drink, breathe, or sleep. Reduce its maximum HP by 1d4 at each dawn, and no effect can stop or reverse this decay. At a maximum of 0 HP, the gemstone breaks and the body dies again. If later raised or resurrected, the character keeps levels and XP earned during the rite’s effect and forgets that period. The hag asks the party to deal with the Pterafolk and may demand a token from Niles Breakbone or Saja N’baza as well.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Tomb of Annihilation, ch. 2, pp. 72–73 (Mbala and the Rite of Stolen Life). The Green Hag rules come from Monster Manual (2014), p. 177.

gm.title: Description
lines: A paladin who bargains with devils can end up leading their troops from the saddle of a nightmare.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Acid, cold. Also bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks made without silvered weapons.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Diabolical Sense. The narzugon has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to notice good-aligned creatures.
Infernal Tack. The narzugon’s spurs let it call its nightmare under the rules in the sidebar.
Magic Resistance. The narzugon has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Use Infernal Command or Terrifying Command and make three Hellfire Lance attacks.
Hellfire Lance. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 11 (1d12 + 5) piercing and 16 (3d10) fire damage. A creature killed by the lance becomes a lemure in the River Styx in Avernus in 1d4 hours. Once that happens, only Wish or slaying the lemure and casting True Resurrection on the original body can bring the creature back. Constructs and devils are immune to this soul effect.
Infernal Command. Allies within 60 ft. cannot be charmed or frightened through the end of the narzugon’s next turn.
Terrifying Command. Non-fiends within 60 ft. that hear the narzugon must make a DC 17 Charisma save or be frightened of it for 1 minute. A target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Passing the save makes it immune to this narzugon’s Terrifying Command for 24 hours.
Healing (1/day). The narzugon or one creature it touches regains up to 100 hit points.

gm.title: Infernal Tack sidebar
lines:
Infernal Tack is a legendary wondrous item that requires attunement by an evil creature. The wearer commands a nightmare already subdued and fitted with the matching tack. Its service lasts until the wearer dies or the tack comes off.
Use an action to clash the spurs or scrape them through blood to call the nightmare. It arrives within 20 ft. at the start of the wearer’s next turn, acts as an ally on the wearer’s initiative count, and stays up to one day. It also departs if either creature dies or the wearer dismisses it as an action. If slain, the nightmare reforms in the Nine Hells within 24 hours and can then be called again.

lines: A six-legged brain collector from the Far Realm. Its head develops a bulge for each stored brain, and after collecting twelve it focuses on finding a way home.

Mind Blast (Recharge 5–6). Choose one Humanoid the collector can see within 10 ft. It makes a DC 14 Wisdom save. On a failure, it takes 9 (2d8) psychic damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half as much damage and avoids incapacitation.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make one Bite attack and one Claws attack.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage and 14 (4d6) poison damage. gm.title: Description
lines: A giant worm that can grow from the last surviving tadpole in an abandoned mind flayer colony. It hunts by sensing nearby minds.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Creature Sense. The neothelid senses creatures with Intelligence 4 or higher within 1 mile. It knows their direction, distance, and Intelligence scores. Mind Blank, Nondetection, or similar magic blocks this sense.
Magic Resistance. The neothelid has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Tentacles. Melee weapon attack, +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 21 (3d8 + 8) bludgeoning damage plus 11 (2d10) psychic damage. A Large or smaller creature must also pass a DC 18 Strength save or be swallowed. The swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the neothelid, and takes 21 (6d6) acid damage at the start of each of the neothelid's turns.
If a creature inside the neothelid deals at least 30 damage to it in one turn, the neothelid makes a DC 18 Constitution save at the end of that turn. On a failure it regurgitates every swallowed creature, and each falls prone within 10 ft. of it. If the neothelid dies, its restraint on swallowed creatures ends. Each can spend 20 ft. of movement to leave the corpse and exits prone.
Acid Breath (recharge 5–6). Each creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 18 Dexterity save, taking 35 (10d6) acid damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

gm.title: Shared spellcasting
lines:
A coven has three hags of any type. All three can use these wizard spells while they are within 30 ft. of one another. Track one pool of spell slots for the whole coven. Each hag casts as a 12th-level spellcaster using Intelligence. This hag uses spell save DC 15 and +7 to hit with spell attacks for this list.
1st level (4 slots): Identify, Ray of Sickness.
2nd level (3 slots): Hold Person, Locate Object.
3rd level (3 slots): Bestow Curse, Counterspell, Lightning Bolt.
4th level (3 slots): Phantasmal Killer, Polymorph.
5th level (2 slots): Contact Other Plane, Scrying.
6th level (1 slot): Eyebite.

gm.title: Hag Eye
lines: A coven can have one Hag Eye. A coven member on the same plane can spend an action to see through it. The eye has AC 10, 1 HP, and darkvision 60 ft. If it is destroyed, each coven member takes 3d10 psychic damage and becomes Blinded for 24 hours. All three hags must perform a 1-hour ritual to make a new eye. They cannot do so while Blinded, and an action outside the ritual makes them start over.

gm.title: Hag Coven
lines: When all three coven members are within 30 ft. of one another, each casts with Intelligence as a 12th-level caster. The coven shares the spell slots. Each hag has save DC 12 plus her Intelligence modifier and spell attack bonus 4 plus that modifier.

gm.title: Description
lines: A night hag puts enemies to sleep, turns allies against each other, or shrinks small enough to haunt a sleeper.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Natural armor. Deception +10, Insight +6, Perception +6, Stealth +7 (+17 with Pass without Trace). Resists fire, necrotic, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from mundane attacks. Immune to Charmed. Darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 16. Common, Infernal, Sylvan.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Stat block and coven action, p. 138.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Supernatural Resistance. Advantage on saves against spells, powers, and other supernatural effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Dream Claw attacks.
Dream Claw. Melee weapon attack +7, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 9 (1d10 + 4) slashing plus 3 (1d6) psychic damage. If this attack hits the same target more than once on a turn, it makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On failure it is Unconscious for up to 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. Damage or another creature in reach using an action to wake it also ends the effect. A creature that cannot be supernaturally put to sleep automatically succeeds.
Vicious Visions (1/day, 6th-level spell). Each creature in a 60-ft. cone makes a DC 15 Wisdom save or is Charmed for 1 minute, ending early if it deals damage to another creature. While Charmed it sees its allies as enemies and its enemies as allies.
Tiny Time. The hag and her gear shrink to 1 inch and become Tiny. She has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide while Tiny and retains her other statistics. As a bonus action she can return to normal size or enter the head of an Unconscious Humanoid within reach. Inside, she has total cover against outside effects and can speak telepathically to the host, which cannot tell where the voice comes from. The host gains no benefit from rest without her permission, and she can give it nightmares as it tries to sleep. Dispel Evil and Good or a similar supernatural effect expels the hag. She can also exit as a bonus action. Either exit restores her normal size.

lines: Sleepwalk. Move one visible Unconscious creature within 60 ft. up to 30 ft. horizontally. Tiny Time also gives the bonus action options in that action.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Aren't You Tired? When a creature within 5 ft. hits the hag, it makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure it cannot take reactions and has disadvantage on attacks and saves through the end of the hag's next turn. A creature that cannot be supernaturally put to sleep is immune.

gm.title: Utility Spells
lines: Charisma, save DC 15. At will, 1 action each: Alter Self, Detect Magic, Pass without Trace. 3/day each, longer casting times: Dream, Legend Lore, Mirage Arcane. 1/day: Scrying using its longer casting time.

gm.title: Description
lines: A creature from the Negative Plane that destroys living things. On the Material Plane, it seeks out places and people tied to the creature it replaced.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder. It also resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Annihilating Aura. Each creature that starts its turn within 30 ft. makes a DC 21 Constitution save or takes 21 (6d6) necrotic damage. Undead are immune.
Life Eater. A creature that the nightwalker reduces to 0 hit points dies. Only Wish can revive it.
Unusual Nature. The nightwalker needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Enervating Focus attacks. Replace one with Finger of Doom if available.
Enervating Focus. Melee weapon attack, +12 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. A hit deals 28 (5d8 + 6) necrotic damage. The target makes a DC 21 Constitution save. On a failure its hit point maximum drops by the necrotic damage taken until it finishes a long rest. If its maximum reaches 0, it dies.
Finger of Doom (recharge 6). Choose one creature the nightwalker can see within 300 ft. The target makes a DC 21 Wisdom save. On a failure it takes 39 (6d12) necrotic damage and is frightened until the end of the nightwalker's next turn. It is paralyzed while frightened this way. A successful save makes the target immune to this nightwalker's Finger of Doom for 24 hours.

gm.title: Negative Plane crossing mechanics
lines: A creature that survives entering the Negative Plane is trapped there as a nightwalker emerges in its place. To escape, it needs the nightwalker lured back with living prey. If the nightwalker is destroyed, the trapped creature cannot escape.

gm.title: Description
lines: A fragment of a goblin trickster god that takes goblin hosts. Fey courts sometimes indulge a goblin jester to keep the spirit from appearing.

gm.title: Traits
lines: Nilbogism. Before trying to damage the nilbog, a creature makes a DC 12 Charisma save. On a failure, it is charmed until the end of its next turn and must use its action to praise the nilbog. The nilbog can regain hit points only by using Reversal of Fortune.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Fool's Scepter. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d6 + 2) bludgeoning damage.
Mocking Word. Choose a creature the nilbog can see within 60 ft. It makes a DC 12 Wisdom save or takes 5 (2d4) psychic damage and has disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Spellcasting
lines:
As an action, cast one listed spell using Charisma (spell save DC 12).
At will. Mage Hand, Tasha's Hideous Laughter.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Nimble Escape. Take the Disengage or Hide action.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Reversal of Fortune. When another creature deals damage to the nilbog, reduce that damage to 0 and regain 3 (1d6) hit points.

gm.title: Nilbog possession mechanics
lines: Without a host, the spirit is invisible, flies 30 ft., cannot be attacked, and is immune to all damage and conditions. On initiative count 20, losing ties, it can only try to possess a goblin within 5 ft. The goblin makes a DC 15 Charisma save. On a failure it is possessed and uses the nilbog stat block. On a success, the spirit cannot possess that goblin for 24 hours. If the host dies or a spell such as Hallow, Magic Circle, or Protection from Evil and Good ends the possession, the spirit seeks another goblin. It can leave voluntarily at any time but does so only if another potential host is nearby. A freed goblin returns to its usual statistics and loses the traits granted by the spirit.

gm.title: Description

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Nilbogism. Before trying to damage the nilbog, a creature must pass a DC 12 Charisma save. On a failure, it is charmed until the end of its next turn and must spend its action praising the nilbog. Reversal of Fortune is the nilbog's only means of regaining hit points, even when magical healing is available.
Nimble Escape. On each of its turns, the nilbog can Disengage or Hide as a bonus action.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:

At will. Mage Hand, Tasha's Hideous Laughter, Vicious Mockery.

gm.title: Actions

Shortbow. Ranged weapon attack, +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. On a hit, deal 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Reversal of Fortune. When another creature deals damage to the nilbog, the nilbog can reduce that damage to 0 and regain 1d6 hit points.

gm.title: Nilbog spirit (possession)
lines: Without a host, the invisible spirit has a flying speed of 30 ft., cannot speak or be attacked, and can take only one kind of action: attempt to possess a goblin within 5 ft. The goblin makes a DC 15 Charisma save. On a failure, its alignment becomes chaotic evil, its Charisma rises to 15 if lower, and it gains Innate Spellcasting, Nilbogism, and Reversal of Fortune from the nilbog stat block. A success prevents this spirit from possessing that goblin for 24 hours. If the host dies or magic ends the possession (such as Hallow, Magic Circle, or Protection from Evil and Good), the spirit looks for another goblin. The spirit can leave at any time but leaves willingly only if it knows of another potential host nearby. A former host reverts to its usual statistics and loses the features granted by the spirit.

gm.title: Camp Vengeance
lines: Parties arriving by boat are ordered to ferry messages and seven sick soldiers downriver to Port Nyanzaru. The soldiers have Blue Mist Fever, Shivering Sickness, or Throat Leeches. Parties arriving over land are ordered to lead four Guards and four Tribal Warriors on a two-week undead patrol back the way they came. Refusal brings arrest and trial. A guilty verdict means confiscation of gear and abandonment in the jungle. Undril Silvertusk can intercede for a party that earned her respect. Otherwise, a sound argument and a successful DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check with each of Ord Firebeard and Perne Salhana can prevent judgment.

lines:
Armor rated AC 7 or worse improves its AC by only 1. It cannot swim, and water washes off its makeup in 1d4 rounds.

Dexterity and morale drop to 3, movement is halved, and it automatically loses initiative. A full turn of continuous exposure kills it in flames. Reflected sunlight, including moonlight or a mirror reflection, deals 1d3 damage without makeup and halves Dexterity and morale. Direct sunlight with 50–99% makeup coverage has the same effects as reflected sunlight.

Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.

gm.title: Description
lines: A nosferatu can return from apparent death in direct moonlight. By day, it relies on servants already under its control.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Fledgling sample, 5th-level human aristocrat. Initiative +8. Touch AC 14, flat-footed AC 22. BAB +3, grapple +4. Space and reach 5 ft. Fort +3, Ref +7, Will +6.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Choose slam +4 melee (1d6 + 1), +1 rapier +8 melee (1d6 + 2, 18–20), or masterwork heavy crossbow +8 ranged (1d10, 19–20/×2).
Domination (Su). Standard action on a target within 30 ft. that the vampire can look at. Will DC 18 or dominate person at caster level 12.
Blood Drain (Ex). Pin a living target in a grapple. Each round the pin holds, drain 1d4 Constitution and gain 5 temporary HP. Each victim of Blood Drain must also make a DC 18 Will save or be dominated until break enchantment succeeds or the vampire dies.
Children of the Night (Su, 1/day). Standard action to call 1d6 + 1 rat swarms, 1d4 + 1 bat swarms, or 3d6 wolves. They arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve for up to 1 hour.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
DR 10/silver and magic, cold and electricity resistance 10, turn resistance +4, spider climb, undead traits. Gaseous form as a standard action at will, with indefinite duration and fly speed 20 ft. (perfect). Alternate Form can assume bat, dire bat, wolf, or dire wolf form. As a standard action assume the listed animal form. Lose the slam and domination, gain the animal’s natural weapons and extraordinary attacks, and retain this form until the next sunrise or another change.
Lunar Regeneration. Direct moonlight converts past damage to nonlethal damage even after apparent death. Heal 3, 4, 6, or 8 per round in crescent, half, gibbous, or full moonlight, plus the age bonus. Fire, acid, and blessed or holy weapons deal normal damage. It can reattach severed limbs. It cannot regenerate a lost limb or recover nonlethal damage with its head detached.
Restful Sleep. While at 1 HP or more, heal 1 HP per HD per hour in its coffin. Daylight disables supernatural abilities. After exposure to direct sunlight, it must sleep in its coffin for 8 hours to restore them. Existing domination persists, and an alternate form cannot end until powers return.

gm.title: Spawn
lines: A humanoid or monstrous humanoid drained to Constitution 0 or less rises on the next full moon. At 4 HD or fewer it becomes spawn, otherwise a nosferatu. Spawn remain controlled until the creator dies. Nosferatu spawn retain charm, gaseous form, spider climb and daylight powerlessness. They heal 2 HP per hour asleep in their coffins if at 1 HP or more, or 2 HP per round in direct full moonlight.

gm.title: Repelling and slaying
lines: Garlic repels it, and a clearly presented holy symbol or mirror keeps it 5 ft. away. It cannot enter a private home without invitation. A stake through the heart kills it while left in place. At 0 HP it collapses but may return in moonlight. Burn the whole body or scatter the severed limbs beyond its minions’ reach. Running water costs one-third of HP each round and destroys it after 3 rounds of immersion.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Bluff +21, Diplomacy +16, Gather Information +11, Hide +12, Intimidate +12, Listen +12, Move Silently +12, Search +13, Sense Motive +15, Spot +12. Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Diplomacy), Weapon Finesse.

gm.title: Encounter adaptation
lines: Apply the strain to the 3.5 vampire template. Retain unmodified abilities, size, BAB, saves and skill points. The base vampire uses undead d12 Hit Dice and has no Constitution score. Keep an existing swim speed and ignore vulnerability to immersion in running water if the base creature can swim. Use save DC 10 + half HD rounded down + Charisma modifier unless specified. Age rows replace one another. Nosferatu lack the base vampire’s Energy Drain. Age DR always requires silver and magic. The cerebral subtype changes the feeding attack only.

gm.title: Age modifiers
lines:
Apply one row to a base creature. The sample already includes its adjustments. Ability scores are listed in Str, Dex, Int, Wis, Cha order.
Fledgling. Abilities 4/4/2/2/6. Speed +0 ft., natural AC +6, turn resistance +4, CR +2. DR 10, lunar healing +0.
Mature. Abilities 4/4/4/2/8. Speed +10 ft., natural AC +6, turn resistance +4, CR +2. DR 15, lunar healing +0.
Old. Abilities 6/6/4/4/8. Speed +10 ft., natural AC +7, turn resistance +5, CR +3. DR 15, lunar healing +1.
Ancient. Abilities 6/6/6/4/10. Speed +20 ft., natural AC +7, turn resistance +6, CR +3. DR 20, lunar healing +1.
Eminent. Abilities 8/8/6/6/10. Speed +20 ft., natural AC +8, turn resistance +7, CR +4. DR 20, lunar healing +2.
Patriarch. Abilities 10/10/8/8/12. Speed +30 ft., natural AC +8, turn resistance +8, CR +5. DR 25, lunar healing +3.

gm.title: Description
lines: This blood-drinking undead keeps the skills and spells of its former life. It can pass for a living person in daylight, though it casts no shadow and has no reflection.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any terrain. Very rare, solitary, and active at any time. Drinks blood. Intelligence 8–18. Treasure F. Any alignment, usually evil. Appearing 1. No magic resistance. Height 5–7 feet. Morale 15–16. The XP listed is the minimum.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite or weapon. One bite deals 1d4 damage. It can instead use a weapon or cast a spell from its former class. Use the THAC0 of the equivalent class and level. Strength is at least 16.
Charm. A creature that meets its gaze saves at −2 or is affected as by charm person. The nosferatu can then use suggestion on that victim.
Change form. It can become gaseous at will and is immune to physical attacks in that form. At night it can become a large bat. By day it can become a raven. It can also use spider climb.
Summon animals. Call 1d100 rats or bats underground, or 3d6 wolves in the wilderness. They arrive in 2d6 rounds.

gm.title: Defenses and defeat
lines:
Only +1 or better magical weapons can harm it. It regains 1 HP each round. Sleep, charm, hold, poison, and paralysis fail against it. Cold and electricity spells deal half damage. At 0 HP it turns gaseous and flees to its coffin. If it fails to reach the coffin within 12 turns, it dies. After eight hours inside, it regains corporeal form.
Garlic repels it. Clerical symbols and holy water are harmless to it. A cleric of opposing alignment or a cleric specialized in hunting undead can turn it. Immersion in running water for three consecutive rounds destroys it. A wooden stake through the heart stops it, but it resumes healing if the stake is removed. To destroy a staked nosferatu permanently, behead it and fill its mouth with earth consecrated to a good deity.

gm.title: Invitation and spawn
lines: A resident must invite it into a private home. Charm or deception can secure the invitation. Once invited, it can come and go. If it chooses to create spawn, a drained human or humanoid rises after three days unless the body is burned or destroyed. The spawn obeys its creator until the creator dies.

gm.title: Former class
lines: Keep the original class’s memories, abilities, skills, and restrictions. Set class level to at least 7 and at most 9 when it becomes a nosferatu. It can advance thereafter at triple the usual XP. Keep ability scores except that Strength is at least 16 and Constitution is no longer required. Warriors and clerics can wear armor without improving AC. Clerics retain spells from their original Immortal patron only if their alignment still matches.

gm.title: Hunger and Red Curse
lines: It must drink at least 9 HP worth of mortal blood per week. After a week of fasting, its ability scores fall by 1 each day to a minimum of 9. An extra 1d4 HP worth of fresh blood restores lost scores. Nonhumanoid blood dulls the pain for one day without restoring scores. It never acquires Legacies and needs no cinnabryl.

lines: Understands one language of its creator but cannot speak.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Constructed Nature. The clockwork needs no air, food, drink or sleep.
Magic Resistance. The oaken bolter has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make two Lancing Bolt attacks or one Lancing Bolt attack and one Harpoon attack.
Lancing Bolt. Melee or ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 100/400 ft., one target. A hit deals 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing damage.
Harpoon. Ranged weapon attack, +7 to hit, range 50/200 ft., one target. A hit deals 9 (1d10 + 4) piercing damage and grapples the target (escape DC 12). Its speed is unchanged, but its own movement must take it closer to the oaken bolter. An escape attempt deals 5 (1d10) slashing damage to the creature whether or not it succeeds. The oaken bolter can hold only one target in this grapple at a time.
Explosive Bolt (Recharge 5–6). Choose a point within 120 ft. Creatures within 20 ft. of it make a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking 17 (5d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Reel In. Pull a creature held by Harpoon 20 ft. closer.

gm.title: Clockwork enhancements
lines:
For an individual clockwork, choose or roll one enhancement and one potential malfunction, both on d10.
1. Camouflaged. Gain Stealth proficiency if needed. While still, the clockwork passes for an inactive machine.
2. Sensors. Raise darkvision to at least 120 ft. and add Perception proficiency if needed.
3. Improved Armor. Increase AC by 2.
4. Increased Speed. Increase speed by 10 ft.
5. Reinforced Construction. Gain resistance to force, lightning and thunder damage.
6. Self-Repairing. At the start of its turn, recover 5 HP if it has at least 1 HP. Lightning damage skips the next recovery.
7. Sturdy Frame. Add its number of Hit Dice to its maximum HP.
8. Suction. Gain a 30-ft. climbing speed.
9. Vocal Resonator. It speaks rudimentary Common or Gnomish, as its maker decides.
10. Water Propulsion. Gain a 30-ft. swimming speed.

gm.title: Clockwork malfunctions
lines:
1. Faulty Sensors. Roll a d6 at turn start. On a 1, the clockwork is blinded until turn end.
2. Flawed Targeting. Roll a d6 at turn start. On a 1, its attack rolls have disadvantage until turn end.
3. Ground Fault. Gain vulnerability to lightning damage.
4. Imprinting Loop. Roll a d6 at turn start. On a 1, it mistakes a visible creature within 30 ft. for its maker. It avoids harming that creature for 1 minute or until the creature attacks or damages it.
5. Leaking Lubricant. Roll a d6 at turn start. On a 1, it gains one level of exhaustion despite immunity.
6. Limited Steering. It moves in straight lines, turning up to 90 degrees before moving and once at the halfway point. It can rotate freely on a turn when it uses none of its speeds.
7. Overactive Sense of Self-Preservation. At the start of a combat turn while at half HP or less, roll a d6. On a 1, the clockwork retreats if it can. If it cannot retreat, it keeps fighting.
8. Overheats. Roll a d6 at turn start. On a 1, it is incapacitated until turn end.
9. Rusty Gears. It has disadvantage on initiative rolls and its speed drops by 10 ft.
10. Weak Armor. Remove its immunity to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage from nonmagical, non-adamantine attacks.

gm.title: Description
lines: Five dead oligarchs still control the Orzhov Syndicate. Karlov breaks ties when the council disagrees.

gm.title: Armor
lines: Natural armor. Each other Obzedat ghost within 30 ft. increases this ghost’s AC by 1.

gm.title: Damage resistances
lines: Acid, cold, fire, lightning, and thunder. The ghost also resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

gm.title: Condition immunities
lines: Charmed, exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, and restrained.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Council of Five. Use the trait for the ghost’s council member.
Ethereal Sight. The ghost can see 60 ft. into the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane and vice versa.
Incorporeal Movement. Creatures and objects count as difficult terrain for the ghost. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Legendary Resistance (1/day). The ghost can turn a failed saving throw into a success.
Undead Nature. The ghost needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.

gm.title: Council of Five
lines:
Enezesku: Enfeebling Ray. Add Ray of Enfeeblement to his at-will innate spells.
Fautomni: Undead Fortitude. If damage drops him to 0 HP, make a Constitution save with a DC of 5 plus the damage taken. On a success he drops to 1 HP. Radiant damage and critical hits bypass this trait.
Karlov: Unnatural Vigor. Whenever he regains HP, he has advantage on attack rolls during his next turn.
Vuliev: Teleportation. Add Misty Step to his at-will innate spells.
Xil Xaxosz: Lingering Spite. When he drops to 0 HP, each creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 16 Constitution save against the burst. Failure deals 14 (4d6) necrotic damage. Success halves the damage.

gm.title: Innate Spellcasting
lines:
The ghost casts with Wisdom (save DC 16, +8 to hit with spell attacks) and needs no components.
At will. Chill Touch, using the 5th-level cantrip damage of 2d8. The ghost regains HP equal to half the damage the target takes.
1/day each. Sanctuary and Spirit Guardians (cast at 4th level).

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Life Drain. Melee weapon attack, +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. A hit deals 18 (4d8) necrotic damage. The ghost regains HP equal to half the damage the target takes. The target must pass a DC 13 Constitution save or reduce its HP maximum by the full damage it took. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if its HP maximum reaches 0.
Convene the Ghost Council. Summon the other four council members. At the start of the summoning ghost’s next turn, they appear in unoccupied spaces within 30 ft. of it and each rolls initiative.

gm.title: Legendary actions
lines:
When all five Obzedat ghosts are within 30 ft. of one another, the council shares a pool of three legendary actions. It can use one option at a time at the end of another creature’s turn. The pool refreshes at the start of the turn of the ghost with the highest initiative.
Forced Obedience (1 action). One target that all five ghosts can see makes a DC 16 Wisdom save. On a failure, the target bows until the end of its next turn. While bowing it cannot take actions or reactions and its speed is 0 and cannot increase.
Indentured Spirits (3 actions). Conjure 1d6 Indentured Spirits within 60 ft. of one of the ghosts.

lines: An odem drains a victim’s judgment before taking control. The host stays aware as the spirit acts through the body.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Any land or underground. Solitary. Always chaotic evil. No treasure. Advancement 6–10 HD (Small). Speaks the languages it knew in life. A viewer who can see ethereal creatures sees a faint white aura around a possessed face.

lines: Initiative +7. AC +1 size, +3 Dex, and +2 deflection. Printed touch 14, flat-footed 13. Base attack +2, printed grapple +2. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +1, Ref +4, Will +6.

lines:
Undead and incorporeal traits and +3 turn resistance.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Attack or full attack. Incorporeal touch +6 melee. A living target hit makes a DC 15 Fortitude save or suffers 1d6 Wisdom drain, which requires magical restoration.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

Bringer of Plagues (Recharge 5–6). Blight a 30-ft.-radius sphere centered on the oinoloth for 24 hours. Normal plants in the area wither and die.
A creature that enters the area or starts its turn there makes a DC 16 Constitution save. On a failure, it takes 14 (4d6) poison damage and is poisoned. On a success, it gains immunity to this oinoloth's Bringer of Plagues for 24 hours.
A creature poisoned this way cannot regain hit points. Every 24 hours, it can repeat the save. Each failure reduces its hit point maximum by 5 (1d10) until the poison ends. The creature dies if its maximum drops to 0. Three successful saves end the poison.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. The olothec breathes air and water.
Immutable Form. Powers, spells, and other effects cannot change its form.
Supernatural Resistance. It has advantage on saving throws against powers, spells, and other supernatural effects.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Multiattack. Make six Devolving Tentacle attacks and use Piscine Transformation.
Devolving Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit 12 (2d6 + 5) piercing damage. The first time a creature is hit by this attack on a turn, it must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution save or be slimed. While slimed it subtracts 1d4 from each attack roll and ability check. After each of its turns, the penalty die steps up from d4 to d6, d8, d10, then d12. A successful repeat save at the end of its turn ends the effect, as do Cure Ailment and Lesser Restoration.
Piscine Transformation (3rd-order power). Choose a visible Humanoid within 60 ft. On a failed DC 17 Wisdom save, change one part of its body. A fish head prevents speech. Fins in place of legs limit walking speed to 10 ft. if it was higher and give a 30-ft. swim speed. A fish torso lets the target breathe only water and hold its breath for 1 hour. If it gains the torso out of water, it starts suffocating. A 4th-order or higher Cure Ailment or Greater Restoration ends a transformation. With all three changes at once, the target permanently becomes a fishlike hybrid. Only Wish or similar magic can restore it then.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Jaunt (3rd-order power). Teleport 30 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space.

gm.title: Lair Actions
lines:
In its lair, take one action from the list on initiative count 20 after any ties. Use a different option from the previous round.
Baleful Teleport. Choose up to two visible creatures within 60 ft. Each that fails a DC 15 Charisma save teleports up to 60 ft. to a visible, unoccupied space of the olothec’s choice.
Psychic Shock. Choose up to two creatures within 30 ft. slimed by Devolving Tentacle. Each takes 9 (2d8) psychic damage. The olothec heals for the total damage dealt.
Slime Eruption. Choose up to three creatures within 120 ft. On a failed DC 15 Constitution save, the target is Poisoned until the end of its next turn.

gm.title: Slime Servant Template
lines: After 1 continuous minute slimed by Devolving Tentacle, the slime ends and the creature loses its memories and becomes an NPC loyal to the olothec. It keeps its statistics and gains amphibious breathing and a swim speed at least equal to its walking speed. It cannot be Charmed or Frightened. The olothec can use its senses and speak through it if it can speak. Only Wish restores its memories and original state.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.
